title: Relevant procedures rank poorly when the search includes a product code
prompt: You have configured a Bedrock Knowledge Base for product support with an OpenSearch Serverless vector store. For a query such as “Procedure for opening the port on TX-403,” a procedure for a different but semantically similar product is ranked higher. Which configuration should you choose to use both product-code matching and the meaning of the question in the search?

choices.text: Make the vector store’s text field nonfilterable and set the search type to HYBRID.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the text-field requirements for HYBRID.

choices.text: Set the search type to SEMANTIC and limit the returned candidates to one.
choices.explanation: Limiting the candidates does not add product-code matching to the search.

choices.text: Provide a filterable text field in the vector store and set the search type to HYBRID.
choices.explanation: A compatible store’s filterable text field can be used to search raw text.

choices.text: Set the search type to SEMANTIC and set the generation temperature to 0.
choices.explanation: Temperature is a generation setting and does not affect the search candidates.

learning.reason: A compatible store’s filterable text field can be used to search raw text.
learning.concept: HYBRID combines vector search with raw-text search.

title: Fewer results are returned than requested for hierarchical chunking
prompt: You split a long operations manual into hierarchical chunks in Bedrock Knowledge Bases. When you request 8 results from the Retrieve API, a search for a short procedure sometimes returns only the body of one section. Ingestion completed successfully, and metadata filters and reranking are disabled. Which explanation accounts for this behavior?

choices.text: With hierarchical chunking, the number of search results is automatically calculated from the token length of the parent chunk.
choices.explanation: The requested count is an upper bound on the child chunks retrieved; it is not calculated from the parent’s token length.

choices.text: With hierarchical chunking, the Retrieve API updates child embeddings for every generation and excludes results while they are being updated.
choices.explanation: The difference in result count for hierarchical search is not caused by embedding updates.

choices.text: Child chunks are searched, and multiple children belonging to the same parent are replaced by their corresponding parent chunk.
choices.explanation: Because multiple results can converge on the same parent chunk, fewer results may be returned than requested.

choices.text: Parent chunks are searched first, and the generation model in use shortens the body to a limit.
choices.explanation: Child chunks are searched first. Retrieve does not generate content.

learning.reason: Because multiple results can converge on the same parent chunk, fewer results may be returned than requested.
learning.concept: Child chunks that share the same parent are replaced by the parent chunk.

title: A deleted internal procedure still appears in search results
prompt: Amazon S3 is connected as a data source for Bedrock Knowledge Bases. A withdrawn procedure was deleted from S3, but its contents still appear as a candidate in users’ searches. What is the minimum action needed to make the deletion take effect in search while preserving the other documents and data source settings?

choices.text: Run Retrieve once, then retry with the same search conditions.
choices.explanation: Retrieve does not update the search index.

choices.text: Delete the knowledge base and vector store, then recreate them from the current S3 bucket.
choices.explanation: Recreating the index and knowledge base is unnecessary.

choices.text: Start a sync on the existing S3 data source and confirm that the ingestion job completes so the deletion is reflected.
choices.explanation: An incremental sync removes items deleted from S3 from the vector store.

choices.text: Enable S3 versioning and add a delete marker to the same key.
choices.explanation: A sync is required to reflect the delete marker’s state in the index.

learning.reason: An incremental sync removes items deleted from S3 from the vector store.
learning.concept: Incremental data source syncs process additions, changes, and individual deletions.

title: Identifying the model for each chapter in a shared manual
prompt: A document containing information about multiple models is split into fixed-size chunks. Each chunk includes a header identifying the corresponding model. The file metadata contains a default model code, but chunk-level model codes should take precedence when users filter by their selected model. Which approach preserves fixed-size chunking in Bedrock Knowledge Bases?

choices.text: Keep fixed-size chunking and use an ingestion-time Lambda custom transformation to add the model code extracted from each header to the chunk-level metadata.
choices.explanation: Lambda can add values to chunks after built-in chunking.

choices.text: Put all model codes in the file-level metadata and have every chunk inherit the same list of models.
choices.explanation: Giving every chunk the same value does not identify the model for each individual chunk.

choices.text: Include the model code in the chunk text and, at search time, apply only an exact-match filter on the file-level metadata with the same name.
choices.explanation: Metadata filters do not evaluate strings that appear in the text.

choices.text: Stop using fixed-size chunking and use instructions to the foundation model to exclude answers about other models.
choices.explanation: This does not preserve fixed-size chunking or provide filtering at search time.

learning.reason: Lambda can add values to chunks after built-in chunking.
learning.concept: Chunk-level metadata takes precedence over a file-level value with the same key.

title: Ingesting a PDF that contains inspection-result images
prompt: Equipment inspection reports are ingested with the default parser in Bedrock Knowledge Bases. Text in the PDFs is searchable, but charts and images embedded in the reports are unavailable. You want to extract the figures and charts during ingestion and store them in S3 so they can be referenced later. Which configuration is appropriate when you do not want to maintain extraction-specific prompts or parser operations code?

choices.text: Keep the default parser and specify HYBRID on the search screen.
choices.explanation: Changing the search method does not add figures and charts that were not extracted.

choices.text: Keep the default parser and increase the maximum token length for chunks.
choices.explanation: Chunk length changes only how text is divided; it does not change extraction capabilities.

choices.text: Specify Amazon Bedrock Data Automation as the parser and configure the S3 bucket for extracted figures and charts.
choices.explanation: An AWS-managed parser can store extracted figures and charts, among other content, in the specified S3 location.

choices.text: Keep the default parser and use a reranker to reorder the search results.
choices.explanation: A reranker reorders candidates that have already been retrieved.

learning.reason: An AWS-managed parser can store extracted figures and charts in the specified S3 location.
learning.concept: A multimodal parser extracts figures, charts, and images from PDFs.

title: Distributing inference destinations within the EU
prompt: An EU support system uses a specific Bedrock model. Processing customer data within the EU is a contractual requirement, and there are no staff available to implement request distribution across Regions. Which actions are needed to meet the requirement when calling the same model from multiple planned EU Regions? Select two.

choices.text: Use the EU geographic cross-Region inference profile supported by that model.
choices.explanation: Bedrock selects an inference destination only within the same geographic scope.

choices.text: Specify the global profile and pin the client to an EU Region.
choices.explanation: Requests to a global profile are not restricted to EU processing destinations, even when sent from the EU.

choices.text: Create an application inference profile based on the global profile in an EU source Region.
choices.explanation: Application-profile usage tracking does not narrow the processing destinations of the underlying profile.

choices.text: List the profile’s processing destinations from each source Region in use and confirm that they are all within the regions covered by the contract.
choices.explanation: The available destinations may differ by source Region, so compare them using GetInferenceProfile.

choices.text: Do not use an inference profile; pin a single-region foundation model ARN in the EU.
choices.explanation: This limits the processing Region but does not automatically distribute requests to the other Regions.

learning.reason: Choose the EU geographic profile and verify that every processing destination for each source is within the contractual scope.
learning.concept: The source Region, processing destinations, and geographic scope of a profile must be considered separately.

title: Importing an Externally Fine-Tuned Model into Bedrock
prompt: A team has a model trained in-house to classify legal documents. In the supported architecture, the final model weights, configuration, and tokenizer are in S3. The team wants to preserve the currently approved weights and make the model available through the Bedrock inference API. Which approach should they choose?

choices.text: Create a Fine-tuning job from input text and labeled examples to customize a foundation model in Bedrock.
choices.explanation: This retrains the parameters of a different model and does not carry forward the approved existing weights.

choices.text: Register the model weights in Knowledge Bases and pass them with the generated prompt on each retrieval.
choices.explanation: Knowledge Bases retrieve data for inference context; they cannot load model weights.

choices.text: Run Custom Model Import with the model artifacts in S3, then perform inference using the imported model's identifier.
choices.explanation: This imports a supported existing model so it can run inference in Bedrock with its trained weights intact.

choices.text: Register the tokenizer in Prompt Management and call it together with a foundation model.
choices.explanation: Prompt configuration cannot replace a foundation model's weights or tokenizer with external artifacts.

learning.reason: When the requirement is to retain an externally trained model, importing it fits better than starting a new training job.
learning.concept: Custom Model Import requires a supported model architecture, artifacts, and model configuration.

title: Processing Individual Large Inference Requests Sequentially
prompt: A dedicated image-captioning model is served with SageMaker AI. Field engineers submit sets of images of about 180 MB whenever needed, and processing takes several minutes. They want to return a request identifier first and let users retrieve the results from S3 once they are ready. They also want to reduce idle costs during overnight periods when there are no requests. Which inference configuration is the best fit?

choices.text: Switch to Serverless Inference, put the images directly in the HTTP body, and wait for a synchronous response.
choices.explanation: This reduces idle costs, but a 180 MB request and processing that takes several minutes exceed the limits of serverless synchronous inference.

choices.text: Use a real-time endpoint and keep the connection open with a streaming response until processing is complete.
choices.explanation: This relies on a persistent connection and does not provide a pattern that accepts requests immediately and writes results to S3 later.

choices.text: Aggregate the day's inputs and run them through Batch Transform, then distribute the results the next morning.
choices.explanation: This works for offline batch processing, but not for processing individual requests as they arrive.

choices.text: Use Asynchronous Inference, specify the S3 input, and enqueue requests; configure the endpoint to scale down to zero instances when idle.
choices.explanation: Asynchronous inference processes large requests and writes results to S3. The endpoint can scale down to zero instances when there are no queued requests.

learning.reason: An asynchronous endpoint with S3 input and output and a request queue meets the requirements for large inputs, multi-minute processing, and individually submitted requests.
learning.concept: Asynchronous inference queues requests and runs long-running inference independently of the response connection.

title: Deploying LoRA Adapters That Share the Same Foundation Model
prompt: Eight departments have each fine-tuned a LoRA adapter for the same public foundation model. They want to select each department's adapter for real-time inference on SageMaker AI. Which two options provide a configuration that lets them update adapters individually without maintaining eight copies of the foundation model?

choices.text: Create a standard inference component for the foundation model and deploy it to a compatible real-time endpoint.
choices.explanation: The foundation model's inference resource can be shared by the adapters.

choices.text: Merge each adapter into the foundation model and deploy eight sets of complete weights in separate model containers.
choices.explanation: This allows independent deployments for each department, but duplicates the same foundation model weights.

choices.text: Place eight different models in production variants of one endpoint and route departments using traffic weights.
choices.explanation: Traffic weights cannot provide department-specific selection and adapter sharing.

choices.text: Associate each department's weights as a separate adapter inference component with the same foundation component.
choices.explanation: Callers can specify an adapter, allowing each adapter to be managed independently without copying the foundation model.

choices.text: Combine all adapters into one S3 object and have every department use the same fixed adapter component.
choices.explanation: This does not provide the distinctions needed to select and update each department's adapter separately.

learning.reason: SageMaker AI adapter inference components are deployed by referencing a standard component for the shared foundation model.
learning.concept: Treat adapter weights and the shared foundation model as separate components.

title: Promoting Only Approved Models to Production
prompt: A pipeline retrains a SageMaker AI model for internal documents every week. Reviewers compare new candidates in staging and want only passing versions to become candidates for production deployment. Which configuration associates the version, training results, and promotion decision, and prevents a retraining run from sending a model to production by itself?

choices.text: Always deploy the latest version from a model package group to production, and roll back to the previous version if a monitoring alarm occurs.
choices.explanation: Monitoring can trigger a rollback, but an unapproved candidate still reaches production.

choices.text: Register each candidate in a Model Registry model package group with PendingManualApproval, then make versions changed to Approved after review eligible for the deployment pipeline.
choices.explanation: This associates evaluation and approval status with a specific model version and lets the status serve as a deployment condition.

choices.text: Use the same endpoint for staging and production, assigning a small traffic share to each new candidate from the outset.
choices.explanation: Even a small traffic share sends the candidate to production inference before review.

choices.text: Overwrite the training artifact at the same S3 key after each retraining run and pass a fixed S3 URI to the production pipeline.
choices.explanation: The artifact changes while the URI stays the same, so the approved version cannot be reliably tied to the deployment artifact.

learning.reason: Separate candidate registration from production promotion, and use only reviewed model package versions as inputs to deployment.
learning.concept: The Model Registry approval status can serve as a deployment gate for each model version.

title: Stop inputs with missing required values before ingestion
prompt: A Parquet file of support inquiries is converted each day into examples for an L2 classification prompt. If blank classification codes or duplicate inquiry IDs slip in, incorrect examples will be used starting the next day. Processing on valid days should continue through the existing Glue job, while an invalid dataset must not be published downstream and the run should notify the team that day. Which approach meets these requirements?

choices.text: Use a Data Catalog crawler to infer the schema, and publish that day's output if the columns are present.
choices.explanation: Detecting that columns exist does not determine whether values are blank or IDs are duplicated.

choices.text: After downstream publication, aggregate the number of prompt responses in CloudWatch and notify the team if it changes sharply from the previous day.
choices.explanation: This does not directly validate input data and sends a notification only after invalid data has been published.

choices.text: Enable Glue job bookmarks to skip S3 objects processed in the previous run.
choices.explanation: Identifying already-processed objects is separate from detecting duplicate IDs within the same dataset.

choices.text: In the Glue job, evaluate DQDL completeness and uniqueness rules before writing. If a required rule fails, stop publication and notify the team of the job failure.
choices.explanation: This evaluates the stated quality conditions for the current batch and can stop processing before data is sent downstream.

learning.reason: Validate input completeness and uniqueness before producing output, and route failures away from the publication path.
learning.concept: AWS Glue Data Quality rule sets can be evaluated during ETL and used as a quality gate.

title: Preserve speaker sides from a two-channel recording
prompt: Support calls are saved in stereo, with the left channel always belonging to the agent and the right channel to the customer. You need to pass timestamped text to a summarization model without mixing the agent's and customer's speech, even when they speak over each other. What is the minimum preprocessing required?

choices.text: Mix the audio into mono and treat every spk_0 label identified by speaker diarization as the agent.
choices.explanation: A speaker label does not establish the speaker's role, and the distinction provided by the original channels is lost.

choices.text: Add “agent” and “customer” to Transcribe's custom vocabulary and generate a single transcript without specifying channels.
choices.explanation: A custom vocabulary can improve recognition of specific words, but it does not identify channels.

choices.text: Assign sentences from a transcript of the mixed channels alternately to the agent and customer, then sort them by speech start time.
choices.explanation: This cannot correctly identify consecutive speech from the same speaker or overlapping speech.

choices.text: Enable channel identification in Amazon Transcribe, then format each channel's transcript and timestamps as model input according to the known channel mapping.
choices.explanation: Transcription is separated by physical channel, allowing the known roles to be mapped to each channel.

learning.reason: Transcribe the audio while preserving its physical channels, then explicitly map the known agent and customer roles to them.
learning.concept: Transcribe channel identification and single-channel speaker diarization have different assumptions.

title: Index only approved content under an S3 prefix
prompt: The same S3 bucket contains published documents under product/current/ and drafts under product/drafts/. Search results must use only the published versions, and drafts must not be stored in the vector store. Synchronization should use the same bucket each time documents are published or replaced. What is the minimum configuration required?

choices.text: Ingest both sets of documents, then exclude drafts at query time using usability metadata.
choices.explanation: This can filter search results, but vectors for the drafts will still be created.

choices.text: Ingest both sets of documents and instruct the model in its prompt not to cite drafts.
choices.explanation: This does not prevent drafts from being indexed or included in the model's context.

choices.text: Set an inclusion prefix of product/current/ for the S3 data source ingestion scope.
choices.explanation: The sync is limited to the specified path, so drafts are not ingested.

choices.text: Sync only /drafts/ and list the published document URIs in the system prompt.
choices.explanation: This ingests only drafts, and listing published document URIs does not create an index of their contents.

learning.reason: When the requirement is to limit the S3 paths synchronized, set the boundary on the data source rather than at query time.
learning.concept: The S3 data source inclusion prefix specifies the ingestion scope.

title: Move to a vector index with the matching embedding dimensions
prompt: An existing OpenSearch Serverless vector field contains 1,536-dimensional Titan G1 vectors. The new environment will use 512-dimensional outputs from Titan Text Embeddings V2. Queries must continue to be accepted by the current environment during migration, while search quality is compared in the new environment. Which actions should you take? Select TWO.

choices.text: Create a separate index with a 512-dimensional vector field and associate it with the new knowledge base's 512-dimensional V2 output.
choices.explanation: The output vector dimensions match the destination field, and the existing index can be retained.

choices.text: Truncate the existing 1,536-dimensional vectors to 512 elements and compare them with queries embedded by V2.
choices.explanation: Truncating vectors does not put them in the same embedding space as V2.

choices.text: Re-embed the source documents with V2 and store them in a new index. Embed search queries with the same model configuration as well.
choices.explanation: This lets document and query vectors be compared in the same model space.

choices.text: Keep using the existing 1,536-dimensional index and add V2's 512-dimensional outputs to the same field.
choices.explanation: The field dimensions do not match the output dimensions.

choices.text: Use V2 to embed only documents that have changed, leaving unchanged documents indexed with G1.
choices.explanation: This would mix vectors from different models and dimensions.

learning.reason: When changing embedding models, create a new index with matching dimensions and a consistent model space.
learning.concept: The vector index dimensions must match the embedding model configuration used for both documents and queries.

title: Separate SQL generation from execution
prompt: An interactive aggregation report is being built. Bedrock Knowledge Bases is already connected to structured data in Redshift. The SQL generated from the submitted natural-language input must not be executed until an operator has reviewed its contents and estimated load. Which API retrieves only the SQL from Bedrock?

choices.text: GenerateQuery
choices.explanation: It converts natural language into SQL for a structured data source, separately from executing the SQL.

choices.text: Retrieve
choices.explanation: When targeting structured data, it returns the results of SQL execution.

choices.text: RetrieveAndGenerate
choices.explanation: It generates an answer using the results of SQL execution.

choices.text: RetrieveAndGenerateStream
choices.explanation: It returns an answer incrementally; it is not an API for running SQL generation on its own.

learning.reason: When the business team must review SQL before deciding whether to use it, GenerateQuery separates SQL generation from retrieval.
learning.concept: For a structured knowledge base, GenerateQuery isolates SQL generation from natural-language input.

title: Delete a data source while retaining data for index reuse
prompt: In a test environment, an S3 data source will be deleted. The vector store will continue to be used by another evaluation system, so the vectors created during ingestion are intentionally to be retained. The original S3 objects must also be retained. Which setting should be configured before deleting the data source?

choices.text: Leave DataDeletionPolicy set to DELETE and enable S3 Versioning.
choices.explanation: S3 object versioning and the deletion behavior of the vector store are independent.

choices.text: Set the data source's DataDeletionPolicy to RETAIN.
choices.explanation: This retains ingested data in the vector store when the data source is deleted.

choices.text: Set DataDeletionPolicy to DELETE, resync the S3 data source, and then delete it.
choices.explanation: Resyncing does not prevent DELETE from deleting the vectors.

choices.text: Set DataDeletionPolicy to DELETE and pin the embedding model version.
choices.explanation: Pinning the model does not affect the deletion policy for generated vectors.

learning.reason: To separate the connector's lifecycle from the retention period of vector data, set the deletion policy to RETAIN.
learning.concept: Updates from syncing source documents and vector retention when deleting a data source are controlled separately.

title: Validate inference setting combinations at deployment time
prompt: An order-summary application manages its model ID, input limit, and allowed-locale combination in AWS AppConfig. The combination must be checked against an external model registry to confirm that the selected model ID supports the locale and limit, and deployment must be stopped if the configuration fails validation. JSON structure validation is already in place. What should be added?

choices.text: Add a model ID string pattern to the JSON Schema and use string structure alone to determine whether it complies with the registry.
choices.explanation: This can validate the ID's structure, but it does not check the limit or supported locales registered in the registry.

choices.text: Add a Lambda validator to the configuration profile that reads the external registry and checks the combination.
choices.explanation: AppConfig deployment-time validation can evaluate conditions that involve external lookups and reject invalid configuration.

choices.text: Use only a deployment strategy that starts at 0%, then roll back if an issue occurs in production.
choices.explanation: Deployment velocity does not validate configuration compatibility in advance.

choices.text: Load the latest value at application startup and switch to a default model if the combination is unsupported at that point.
choices.explanation: The inconsistent configuration would still be deployed and retrieved, so it would not be rejected before deployment.

learning.reason: Use deployment-time Lambda validation for consistency conditions involving external systems that are difficult to express in a static schema.
learning.concept: An AppConfig Lambda validator can check consistency between configuration content and external state.

title: Separate production prompts from prompts under editing
prompt: A maintenance team updates system instructions daily using Bedrock Prompt Management. The goal is to reproduce only configurations approved by the validation team in production, without allowing work in progress to leak into production. The team must be able to continue editing the pre-approval variant in the same prompt. Which action is appropriate?

choices.text: Create a prompt version from the approved state and pin the production configuration to that version's ARN.
choices.explanation: A version is a snapshot of the prompt at creation time and can be used independently of draft changes.

choices.text: Keep production pointed at DRAFT and monitor the results whenever developers make changes.

choices.text: Pin the ARN of the foundation model in use and retrieve the latest draft of the prompt each time.
choices.explanation: Pinning the model version does not prevent changes to the instructions.

learning.reason: Promote a validated configuration as an immutable prompt version, while continuing editing work in the draft.
learning.concept: A Prompt Management version fixes the prompt contents as they were when the version was created.

title: Set search filters for each CSV row
prompt: A single CSV stores support procedures, one per row. You want to search the natural-language text in the instruction column and filter results by product and market, which vary within the same CSV. Keep the CSV in S3 as is, without adding a separate transformation process. What should you configure?

choices.text: Put every product and market value in arrays in file-level metadata.

title: Verify a Response Against an Employee Benefits Policy
prompt: Internal guidance is delivered in U.S. English in a single response. A policy formalizes eligibility requirements for employee benefits. If a generated answer conflicts with those requirements, you want to record the evidence and route it to a reviewer. Which combination of Guardrails capabilities and application-side processing should you use? Select TWO.

choices.text: Add key terms from the rules to a word filter, and treat every term match as a logical contradiction of the eligibility requirements.
choices.explanation: A prohibited-term match does not determine whether the relationships among requirements or exceptions to their application are correct.

choices.text: Configure the requirements as an Automated Reasoning policy and evaluate the completed answer against that policy.
choices.explanation: The evaluation follows the variables and rules expressed in the policy and returns structured findings about contradictions or missing assumptions.

choices.text: Enable only the standard content filters in Guardrails and expect them to add evidence for the specified eligibility requirements to the response.
choices.explanation: Content-filter results do not formally evaluate an organization's employee benefits policy.

choices.text: Stream the inference and forward each received token directly to the user while Automated Reasoning verifies it incrementally.
choices.explanation: The evaluation requires a completed response, and Automated Reasoning does not support streaming APIs.

choices.text: Have the application interpret the findings and route the answer to a reviewer instead of returning it to the user when there is a contradiction or specified uncertainty.
choices.explanation: Findings are inputs for application decisions, and the application can route contradictions into its own approval workflow.

learning.reason: Evaluate a formalized policy with Automated Reasoning, then have the application use the findings to decide whether to route the answer for review.
learning.concept: Automated Reasoning returns findings about a policy. The application must separately implement any processing based on those findings.

choices.text: Move to batch inference and stream interactive requests sequentially.
choices.explanation: Batch inference is asynchronous offline processing and is not suitable for securing capacity for high-priority interactive requests.

choices.text: Consider Provisioned Throughput or a Reserved Tier for the target model after confirming availability.
choices.explanation: Correct. For predictable, sustained throughput requirements, AWS recommends considering Provisioned Throughput or a Reserved Tier for supported models.

choices.text: Retry all requests at the same time to secure on-demand capacity.
choices.explanation: Synchronized retries can worsen capacity contention.

choices.text: Increase the S3 bucket used for logs to allocate inference capacity.
choices.explanation: A log destination does not reserve service capacity for model inference.

learning.reason: For predictable, sustained throughput requirements, AWS recommends considering Provisioned Throughput or a Reserved Tier after confirming support.
learning.concept: Choosing reserved capacity for predictable generative AI workloads

category: テスト・検証・トラブルシューティング
examDomain: テスト・検証・トラブルシューティング
title: Evaluating subjective writing quality with human reviewers
prompt: You are comparing two model candidates that generate drafts of legal documents. You want legal professionals to assess readability and business usefulness from their perspective, and you also want to collect evaluator annotations. Which Amazon Bedrock Model Evaluation method is most appropriate?

choices.text: Use automated evaluation only, without specifying human evaluation criteria.
choices.explanation: Automated evaluation is useful, but it does not directly collect legal professionals’ subjective business judgments.

choices.text: Immediately route half of production users to each candidate and adopt one before evaluation.
choices.explanation: This allows a comparison, but adopting a model in production before evaluation and approval leaves a quality risk.

choices.text: Use a human model evaluation job to collect judgments from human reviewers against defined evaluation criteria.
choices.explanation: Correct. Subjective qualities such as readability and practical usefulness can be compared through human evaluation against explicitly defined criteria.

choices.text: Judge writing quality using only the number of CloudWatch invocations.
choices.explanation: Invocation volume does not measure writing style or business usefulness.

learning.reason: Model Evaluation offers human and automated evaluation; subjective quality criteria can be assessed by human reviewers.
learning.concept: Human model evaluation for subjective generative quality

category: テスト・検証・トラブルシューティング
examDomain: テスト・検証・トラブルシューティング
title: Evaluating answer correctness against reference answers
prompt: You are comparing generated answers to regulatory FAQs before and after an update. The evaluation data includes a legally reviewed reference answer for each question, and your primary goal is to quantify consistently whether the answers are correct. Which built-in LLM-as-a-Judge metric is most direct?

choices.text: Choose ProfessionalStyleAndTone alone and treat a polite tone as evidence of correctness.
choices.explanation: A professional style can be measured, but it does not measure whether the regulatory content is correct.

choices.text: Compare only input token counts and treat shorter answers as correct.
choices.explanation: Token volume does not evaluate content correctness.

choices.text: Choose Correctness and use the evaluation dataset’s reference answers in the evaluation.
choices.explanation: Correct. Correctness measures whether a response is correct, and the evaluation model considers reference answers when they are included in the dataset.

choices.text: Measure only average response time and treat the faster model as more accurate.
choices.explanation: Latency and the correctness of regulatory answers are separate quality characteristics.

learning.reason: Correctness measures response correctness and takes reference answers in the prompt dataset into account when they are available.
learning.concept: LLM-as-a-Judge Correctness evaluation using reference answers

category: テスト・検証・トラブルシューティング
examDomain: テスト・検証・トラブルシューティング
title: Isolating a 400 input-contract violation
prompt: After a new release, calls to the Bedrock API consistently return 400 ValidationError. There is no network outage or increase in request volume, and every failed request includes the same new field. What should you investigate first?

choices.text: Keep resending the same request with exponential backoff.
choices.explanation: Backoff addresses transient capacity or throttling issues; it does not fix deterministic invalid input.

choices.text: Check the required parameters, value ranges, and formats for the API being used, and make the new field conform to the request contract.
choices.explanation: Correct. ValidationError indicates that input does not meet constraints such as required parameters, allowed ranges, or formats.

choices.text: Immediately request a service quota increase.
choices.explanation: Quota exhaustion typically causes ThrottlingException, not 400 ValidationError.

choices.text: Delete and recreate the destination S3 bucket.
choices.explanation: This does not correct a violation of the API input constraints.

learning.reason: ValidationError occurs when a request does not meet the API’s required parameters, formats, allowed ranges, or other constraints.
learning.concept: Validating the request contract based on the Bedrock API error type

category: テスト・検証・トラブルシューティング
examDomain: テスト・検証・トラブルシューティング
title: Investigate Failed Invocations with Large Inputs and Outputs
prompt: Generated results differ from expectations only when the input is long and includes images. You want to investigate the issue later, including the invocation payload, but CloudWatch Logs events cannot fully store large binary data or JSON payloads larger than 100 KB. Which logging configuration is most appropriate?

choices.text: Use CloudWatch Logs alone and always embed payloads larger than 100 KB in the same event.
choices.explanation: Large payloads and binary data cannot be stored completely in a CloudWatch Logs event; delivery to S3 is needed.

choices.text: Enable CloudTrail and reconstruct all model input images from management events.
choices.explanation: CloudTrail is not designed to store model input and output payloads for investigation.

choices.text: Disable logging and collect only screen recordings from users.
choices.explanation: This does not allow systematic comparison of the actual invocation contents and metadata.

choices.text: Configure large-data delivery to Amazon S3 with model invocation logging, and use CloudWatch Logs metadata together with references to the payloads in S3.
choices.explanation: Correct. Large JSON payloads and binary data are stored in S3, and the log record can reference their location.

learning.reason: Large JSON payloads and binary data are stored as separate objects in S3, and the log record contains a reference to each object's location.
learning.concept: Traceability for large multimodal invocations

category: テスト・検証・トラブルシューティング
examDomain: テスト・検証・トラブルシューティング
title: Create a Custom Evaluation Dataset for Your Business
prompt: You want to repeatedly compare summary quality for your organization's inquiry format using automatic model evaluation. Built-in datasets do not cover your business terminology. Which preparation is correct for a custom prompt dataset?

choices.text: Select CloudWatch Logs events directly as the evaluation dataset.
choices.explanation: CloudWatch Logs is not an input format for a custom evaluation dataset.

choices.text: Concatenate all prompts into the first row of a CSV file and provide it without an S3 URI.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the evaluation job's JSONL and S3 URI input requirements.

choices.text: Wait for the evaluation job to collect production invocations automatically, without specifying test data.
choices.explanation: Automatic evaluation uses a selected built-in dataset or a specified custom dataset.

choices.text: Place a .jsonl file in S3 with a valid JSON object on each line, then specify its S3 URI in the evaluation job.
choices.explanation: Correct. A custom prompt dataset for automatic model evaluation must be in JSONL format in S3, with each line containing a valid JSON object.

learning.reason: A custom prompt dataset must be JSONL stored in S3, and every line must contain a valid JSON object.
learning.concept: Prompt datasets for business-specific regression evaluation

category: テスト・検証・トラブルシューティング
examDomain: テスト・検証・トラブルシューティング
title: Reliably Test an Updated Agent
prompt: After changing an action group configuration in Bedrock Agents Classic, the test results appear to show old behavior. Select two actions needed to test the changed configuration and determine at which stage an unintended action selection occurs.

choices.text: Refer only to the previous test results and treat the changed configuration as current without running PrepareAgent.
choices.explanation: Previous results do not guarantee that the new working draft has been prepared.

choices.text: Compare only CloudWatch charges to determine which action was selected.
choices.explanation: Charges do not directly show action selection or the reasoning process.

choices.text: Check preparedAt from GetAgent and verify that the agent was prepared with PrepareAgent after the change.
choices.explanation: Correct. AWS recommends checking preparedAt before testing to confirm that you are testing the latest configuration.

choices.text: Delete and recreate the agent every time, and disable traces.
choices.explanation: Deleting the agent is not a way to verify an updated configuration, and disabling traces removes information needed for diagnosis.

choices.text: Display the test session's trace and inspect the reasoning configuration, action group usage, and each step.
choices.explanation: Correct. A trace shows each stage of orchestration and action usage, helping isolate an unintended selection.

learning.reason: For Agents Classic testing, preparedAt can confirm that the latest configuration is prepared, and the trace shows the stages involving reasoning, actions, and knowledge bases.
learning.concept: Verifying agent preparation after an update and troubleshooting with traces

category: テスト・検証・トラブルシューティング
examDomain: テスト・検証・トラブルシューティング
title: Use an Evaluation Metric to Detect Reduced Instruction Following
prompt: For generated product descriptions, the main problem is not factual inaccuracy but failure to follow explicit instructions such as “no more than five bullet points” and “do not mention the price.” Which built-in metric most directly addresses this objective in model evaluation using LLM-as-a-Judge?

choices.text: Select only Faithfulness.
choices.explanation: Faithfulness measures whether a response includes information that is not in the available context; it does not directly measure compliance with formatting or prohibited-content instructions.

choices.text: Select Following instructions.
choices.explanation: Correct. This metric measures how well a response follows the precise instructions in the prompt.

choices.text: Select only the input token count.
choices.explanation: Token volume does not evaluate whether instructions were followed.

choices.text: Select only latency.
choices.explanation: A fast response does not mean it followed the bullet-count limit or the prohibition.

learning.reason: FollowingInstructions evaluates how well a response follows the precise instructions stated in the prompt.
learning.concept: Matching a quality issue to a model evaluation metric with LLM-as-a-Judge

category: テスト・検証・トラブルシューティング
examDomain: テスト・検証・トラブルシューティング
title: Identify which endpoints are covered by model invocation logging
prompt: During an incident investigation, you enabled Model invocation logging, but some newer OpenAI-compatible API calls are not being recorded. The configuration is correct in the same account and Region, and the calls are sent to the bedrock-mantle endpoint. Which assessment of the cause is most appropriate?

choices.text: Configure high-volume data delivery to the log S3 bucket so that calls to any endpoint are recorded.
choices.explanation: High-volume data delivery supplements the destination for request and response bodies; it does not expand endpoint coverage.

choices.text: Model invocation logging covers calls made through the bedrock-runtime endpoint, so the same API calls through bedrock-mantle are not currently recorded.
choices.explanation: Correct. Bedrock model invocation logging covers supported calls made through the bedrock-runtime endpoint.

choices.text: Set the CloudWatch Logs retention period to unlimited to recover calls that were not recorded in the past.
choices.explanation: Retention applies to logs already delivered; it does not record calls to an unsupported endpoint retroactively.

choices.text: Keep the input token count below 100 KB to enable logging for any endpoint.
choices.explanation: Body size can affect the log representation, but it does not change the endpoint eligibility condition.

learning.reason: Model invocation logging covers supported operations through the bedrock-runtime endpoint, not calls through other endpoints such as bedrock-mantle.
learning.concept: Distinguishing logging coverage in generative AI observability.

category: 基盤モデルの統合・データ管理・コンプライアンス
examDomain: 基盤モデルの統合・データ管理・コンプライアンス
title: Split the comparison dimensions in a compound query
prompt: A user asks to compare the warranty periods of products A and B in the same question, but Bedrock RetrieveAndGenerate repeatedly retrieves documents for only one of them. You confirmed that searching for each product name separately returns the correct documents. Without changing the maximum number of results per search, which option lets managed orchestration handle both?

choices.text: Set queryTransformationConfiguration to QUERY_DECOMPOSITION so that partial queries are created from the compound question and searched.
choices.explanation: The compound query is split before generation, allowing the system to try to retrieve evidence from different sources.

choices.text: Increase the maximum output tokens in generationConfiguration to produce a longer comparison answer.
choices.explanation: A longer answer does not resolve the situation where the initial search retrieved documents for only one product.

choices.text: Add a single-document filter to vector search that requires both product codes.
choices.explanation: If each product is covered by a separate document, there may be no single document containing both codes, so relevant evidence can be missed.

choices.text: Rerank the existing candidates and answer using only the top results.
choices.explanation: Reordering candidates cannot retrieve the document for the other product if it was not in the initial search results.

learning.reason: Because searches for each product separately are known to work, split the compound question into separate search units.
learning.concept: QUERY_DECOMPOSITION splits compound queries during RetrieveAndGenerate orchestration before retrieval.

title: Use an existing Kendra index directly as a knowledge base
prompt: Internal documents are already ingested and searched through an existing Amazon Kendra GenAI index. You want to build Bedrock Knowledge Bases with IaC and do not want to add infrastructure for copying data to a separate vector store or for re-ingestion. Which two actions are needed during setup, while granting Bedrock only the minimum required permissions to Kendra? Select two.

choices.text: Initialize a new Kendra index in the same CreateKnowledgeBase request and automatically move documents from the existing index.
choices.explanation: For a Kendra-type knowledge base created through the API, the index must be prepared in advance. This also conflicts with the requirement to keep using the existing document workflow.

choices.text: Export all index search results and build a new ingestion pipeline with S3 and OpenSearch Serverless.
choices.explanation: This would create a separate search and ingestion setup alongside the existing index.

choices.text: Specify the existing Kendra GenAI index when creating the Bedrock knowledge base.
choices.explanation: When creating a Kendra-type knowledge base through the API, you can reference an existing GenAI index.

choices.text: Write the Kendra index ARN as a string in the body of a Prompt Management template.
choices.explanation: Putting an identifier in a template does not associate it with a retrieval source.

choices.text: Grant the knowledge base service role the required access to the target Kendra index.
choices.explanation: This lets Bedrock use the specified index without granting the user broad index permissions.

learning.reason: Create a knowledge base that references the existing GenAI index, then grant the service role permission to use that index.
learning.concept: Bedrock Knowledge Bases connected to a Kendra GenAI index can directly reference an existing index.

title: Deploy an approved model to another account
prompt: A model is tuned and approved in a machine learning account, then deployed to SageMaker AI in a production account. The approved model version references S3 artifacts and an ECR inference image, which must be used without copying them; only the production deployment role will use them. Include the KMS key used for the artifacts in the sharing scope. What should you do?

choices.text: Share only the model group with the production account and inherit S3 and ECR permissions from the group.
choices.explanation: Access granted to the model group is evaluated separately from permissions for the referenced S3 and ECR resources.

choices.text: Add an IAM policy from the training account with the same name to the production deployment role, without setting resource policies on the source side.
choices.explanation: This omits permissions from the source account for access to its cross-account resources.

choices.text: Set cross-account permissions on the model group, the artifact S3 bucket, and the image in ECR, and grant the deployment role the required SageMaker actions and KMS use.
choices.explanation: In addition to the model group, S3, and ECR, permission for the production role to use the original KMS key is required. Verify authorization on the key side through a key policy or grant, along with the effective permissions of the consuming role.

choices.text: Create a new KMS key in the production account and specify only that key to read the original encrypted artifacts.
choices.explanation: A different key cannot decrypt artifacts encrypted with the original key, and this does not resolve permissions for S3 or ECR.

learning.reason: In addition to permission to access the model version, align permissions for the artifacts, image, and decryption.
learning.concept: SageMaker Model Registry sharing permissions are not automatically inherited by the referenced S3, ECR, or KMS resources. For KMS, align authorization on the key side through a key policy or grant with the effective permissions of the production role that uses it.

title: Providing business-term and SQL examples as generation context
prompt: In a structured knowledge base connected to Redshift, the model generates the wrong expiration condition when asked about a business term meaning “active contract.” You want to improve SQL generation using only the defined dataset, without renaming columns or replacing the application’s queries with fixed SQL. What should you configure? Select two.

choices.text: Extend the maximum query time only for requests containing that business term.
choices.explanation: Adjusting the timeout does not change the condition in the generated WHERE clause.

choices.text: Add descriptions to the relevant columns or tables explaining their business meaning and applicable conditions.
choices.explanation: SQL generation can then use both the data structure and the meaning of the terms.

choices.text: Exclude the columns corresponding to existing business terms from the generation scope.
choices.explanation: This makes required fields unavailable and makes it harder to generate the correct condition.

choices.text: Add examples pairing natural-language questions with reviewed SQL as curatedQueries.
choices.explanation: Concrete examples can show the model the relationship between business terms and the queries it should generate.

choices.text: After executing incorrect SQL, lower the summary temperature so the correct expiration condition is displayed.
choices.explanation: Generation settings applied after SQL execution cannot correct the data or conditions used by the query.

learning.reason: Improve the SQL-generation context by providing business meanings for columns and examples of the desired query patterns.
learning.concept: Descriptions for structured knowledge bases and curated queries can improve SQL generation accuracy.

title: Preserving source citations with a custom template
prompt: A maintenance-support application uses Bedrock RetrieveAndGenerate, and you introduced a custom prompt that formats answers as short bullet points. The search results contain the expected documents, and the response body reflects their facts, but the citations shown with the default template have disappeared. What should you do to restore built-in citations while keeping the answer in bullet points?

choices.text: Keep the placeholder that passes the search results into the custom template, and restore the citation-related $output_format_instructions$ in the template configuration.
choices.explanation: This passes both the retrieved context and the instructions needed for the service’s citation format.

choices.text: Increase the number of search results and omit the citation placeholder from the template.
choices.explanation: More search results do not supply the missing citation-format instructions.

choices.text: Remove $search_results$ and simply tell the model in the body to cite the documents it finds.
choices.explanation: This removes the part of the prompt that passes the retrieved content to the model.

choices.text: Keep the current template, increase the model’s maximum output, and request citation data in the response after generation.
choices.explanation: A longer output limit does not restore the template variable required to generate citations.

learning.reason: When citations disappear after changing a custom template, pass both the retrieved documents and the built-in citation instructions appropriately.
learning.concept: Bedrock Knowledge Bases requires $output_format_instructions$ for source citations.

category: 基盤モデルの統合・データ管理・コンプライアンス

title: Identifying duplicate records with different identifiers before ingestion
prompt: You are extracting vocabulary and examples for generative AI from support histories in multiple systems. The same companies appear under different abbreviations or address formats, and there is no customer ID shared across the systems. Rather than delete records, you want to group likely duplicates for staff to review. Staff have labeled which records refer to the same company, and you use an existing AWS Glue ETL job. What should you do?

choices.text: Use DQDL to check that company names are unique by exact match, and classify all differently named records as separate companies.
choices.explanation: An exact-match check does not associate different representations of the same company.

choices.text: Tune a FindMatches transform using labeled matching examples, and configure it to output match_id so that groups of rows identified as the same company are retained.
choices.explanation: Record matching trained from examples can group candidates for review even without an exact-match ID.

choices.text: Sort only by company name in phonetic order, then mechanically delete adjacent records as belonging to the same company.
choices.explanation: This does not use the reviewed labels or addresses, and it does not preserve candidates for evidence-based review.

choices.text: Use only file-based Glue job bookmarks and retain the different company names from each input system.
choices.explanation: Bookmarks track processed files; they do not match different records.

learning.reason: Use labeled examples to learn matches across variant spellings, then present the groups to staff without dropping rows.
learning.concept: FindMatches can match records without an exact-match key and output match_id for review.

title: Standardizing proper product names in transcription results
prompt: You are preparing training audio for use as summarization data. Overall transcription accuracy is sufficient, but a particular product name is recognized as a similar-sounding common word, and the transcript contains spellings that differ from your company’s standard. The problem is limited to 20 terms, and the terms can be managed in the Region used for transcription. How can you fix this without training a new language model for the entire corpus?

choices.text: Create a custom vocabulary table in Amazon Transcribe, specify Phrase and DisplayAs, and apply the vocabulary to the transcription job.
choices.explanation: A custom vocabulary can improve recognition of specific terms and specify how they appear in the transcript.

choices.text: Enable channel identification in the audio and have each channel return the same product name.
choices.explanation: This setting separates conversation channels; it does not specify term recognition or output spelling.

choices.text: Train a new custom language model to improve recognition across the full context, without specifying how the product name should be displayed.
choices.explanation: This is broader than adapting to the context of the entire corpus and does not directly assign the required spelling.

choices.text: After transcription, replace only exact matches of the product name in the text.
choices.explanation: If it was misrecognized as a different common word, the specified product name will not appear in the transcript to replace.

learning.reason: When recognition and spelling issues are limited to specific terms, configure their display forms in a custom vocabulary at transcription time.
learning.concept: An Amazon Transcribe custom vocabulary table can tune recognition and displayed spelling for selected terms.

category: 基盤モデルの統合・データ管理・コンプライアンス

title: Choosing Search Attributes from Natural-Language Queries
prompt: In a search experience for public manuals, users enter natural-language filters such as “models from 2025 onward in North America.” The data already has typed metadata for market and modelYear, and all users can view the same materials. You want to infer metadata conditions from the query before retrieval, without adding filter fields to the interface. Which actions should you take? Select two.

choices.text: Define each metadata key, type, and meaning in metadataAttributes, then configure implicit filtering.
choices.explanation: The model can use the available attributes, their meanings, and their types to generate the filters that correspond to a query.

choices.text: Add descriptions of market and modelYear only to the prompt template for the generation model, without changing the retrieval configuration.
choices.explanation: Vector retrieval occurs before the answer is generated, and the prompt template alone does not change the conditions used during retrieval.

choices.text: Overwrite metadata values directly from users’ search terms, then leave filtering unconfigured.
choices.explanation: This confuses a document’s actual attributes with the conditions in a query.

choices.text: Specify the ARN of a model that supports implicit filtering.
choices.explanation: You must specify the model used to construct the filters.

choices.text: Infer new metadata attributes for the entire set of retrieved results after generation is complete.
choices.explanation: That would be too late to filter the results before retrieval.

learning.reason: Give the model a contract for the existing document metadata so it can construct attribute conditions from natural-language queries, without adding to the document metadata.
learning.concept: Implicit metadata filtering predicts conditions at retrieval time. It is separate from authorization requirements.

title: Ingesting PDFs While Preserving Source Page Numbers
prompt: A 300-page procedure manual is stored as a PDF in Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases. It was ingested using a configuration that creates one chunk per document. Users have asked to see the page number for each citation and to filter for results from a specific page. You want to keep OpenSearch Serverless and avoid splitting PDFs yourself or registering page numbers manually. What should you do?

choices.text: Keep the no-chunking configuration and instruct the generation prompt to infer page numbers.
choices.explanation: Page numbers are not attached during ingestion, so they cannot be used as retrieval filters.

choices.text: Manually assign a fixed pageNumber to each PDF S3 object and keep using no chunking.
choices.explanation: A document-level value cannot identify the individual source page within a 300-page PDF.

choices.text: Enable only runtime reranking and leave the existing chunks unchanged.
choices.explanation: This can change the order of retrieved results, but it does not add page-number metadata.

choices.text: Reingest the PDF with a built-in chunking configuration that supports page-number metadata, instead of using no chunking.
choices.explanation: With a supported vector store and chunking configuration, page-number metadata derived from PDFs is available.

learning.reason: To preserve page-level evidence, use an ingestion-time chunking configuration that retains page numbers.
learning.concept: PDF page-number metadata is not supported with no chunking.

category: 基盤モデルの統合・データ管理・コンプライアンス

title: Invoking a Fine-Tuned Model Without Reserved Capacity
prompt: Fine-tuning has been completed in Amazon Bedrock, and the model and Region support custom-model on-demand deployments. Inference for search assistance is minimal at night and on weekends. Which actions let you use the same weights without fine-tuning the model again or reserving provisioned capacity? Select two.

choices.text: Specify the ID of the base foundation model used to create the model; the most recently fine-tuned weights will be selected automatically.
choices.explanation: The base model ID does not identify the fine-tuned deployment.

choices.text: Specify the ARN of the fine-tuned custom model and create a custom-model on-demand deployment.
choices.explanation: You can associate an existing custom model with a deployment for on-demand inference.

choices.text: Reserve the minimum unit of Provisioned Throughput and associate the fine-tuned model with it.
choices.explanation: Even if the configuration supports the fine-tuned model, it does not meet the requirement to avoid reserving capacity.

choices.text: Specify the training job ARN as the model and rerun the training job to obtain inference results.
choices.explanation: A training job is not the identifier of an inference deployment.

choices.text: When the deployment is Active, specify the deployment’s ARN as modelId for inference.
choices.explanation: Invoke inference using the ARN of the on-demand deployment, not the identifier of the custom model itself.

learning.reason: Deploy the custom model for on-demand use, then use the ARN of the deployed resource at runtime.
learning.concept: A Bedrock custom model and a custom-model deployment have different identifiers for creation and inference.

title: Integrating a Marketplace Model into an Existing Bedrock Application
prompt: An existing inquiry-classification application invokes models through Amazon Bedrock. A third-party model approved internally is listed in the Bedrock Marketplace catalog. The solution must use the company’s SageMaker AI execution role and instance types, and the contract cannot be changed to send data to a separate external API. How should you integrate the model?

choices.text: Specify the Marketplace product-page URL as modelId in Bedrock Converse.
choices.explanation: A catalog URL is not the identifier of a running inference endpoint.

choices.text: Invoke the undeployed Marketplace model using the ARN of a separate on-demand foundation model.
choices.explanation: That ARN identifies a different foundation model and cannot invoke the selected Marketplace model.

choices.text: Save the documentation to Amazon S3 and sync it to Knowledge Bases to start inference with the catalog-listed model.
choices.explanation: Creating a retrieval index through ingestion is different from deploying a Marketplace model endpoint.

choices.text: Deploy the model to a compatible SageMaker AI endpoint from Bedrock Marketplace, then use the ready endpoint through Bedrock.
choices.explanation: You can deploy a Marketplace model to a SageMaker AI inference resource and integrate it into the Bedrock invocation path.

learning.reason: Deploy the catalog model to an available runtime environment, then make it an inference target through Bedrock.
learning.concept: Deploy Bedrock Marketplace models to SageMaker AI endpoints before using them.

title: Serve a fleet of models with varying usage on the same endpoint
prompt: You need to serve 50 industry-specific classification models with SageMaker AI. All models use the same supported framework, and they do not share weights. Only some models are called frequently, and latency while loading an infrequently used model is acceptable. Which configuration lets the caller select a model based on industry information without keeping every model on a dedicated instance?

choices.text: Place the models on a multi-model endpoint, specify the target model in each invocation, and load it into memory as needed.
choices.explanation: This shares the inference container and resources while loading the requested model in response to demand.

choices.text: Add the 50 models separately as LoRA adapters to a single model, assuming they can share weights.
choices.explanation: The weights of independent, complete models cannot simply be replaced with LoRA adapters on a shared base model.

choices.text: Keep every model running as a production variant and use weights to assign invocations at random.
choices.explanation: This does not provide reliable model selection based on industry information or reduce the cost of keeping infrequently used models ready.

choices.text: Place all models in a sequential inference pipeline and return the result from the final model.
choices.explanation: This is different from selecting the one model needed to process each request.

learning.reason: Independent models can share the same serving environment, with only the model in use loaded into memory as needed.
learning.concept: SageMaker multi-model endpoints let you share resources while accepting load latency for infrequently used models.

title: Change production traffic between two models through endpoint configuration
prompt: An existing SageMaker AI endpoint serves an old and a new model version as two production variants. The application currently sends most requests to the old version without specifying TargetVariant for individual requests. Approval has been given to increase the new version's share. How can you change the traffic allocation on the current endpoint without changing the application or model artifacts?

choices.explanation: This can explicitly pin requests to a variant, but it requires an application change.

choices.text: Update the desired weights of both production variants with UpdateEndpointWeightsAndCapacities.
choices.explanation: This changes how requests that do not specify an individual variant are distributed at the current endpoint.

choices.text: Change only the model package approval status and wait for traffic to shift to the new version automatically.
choices.explanation: The registry approval status does not change inference routing on an existing endpoint.

choices.text: Overwrite the S3 key for the old model artifact with the new version's weights.
choices.explanation: This does not change the traffic proportions between active variants and makes version tracking more difficult.

learning.reason: Keep the models deployed on the existing endpoint and adjust the weights used for routing.

choices.text: Add a PDF in a document block in a Converse message, but omit a text block from that message.

choices.text: Pass an S3 URL as text in a system block and let the model download the PDF automatically.

choices.text: Incrementally sync all PDFs to a shared Knowledge Base and search it for each user's question.
choices.explanation: This would store one-off inputs in a shared search index, contrary to the requirement.

learning.reason: For one-off document processing, put the document block and the instructions block in the same user message in Converse.

choices.text: Create one Condition node for each row.
choices.explanation: This does not support a dynamically sized array.

choices.text: Concatenate all rows into the model ID.
choices.explanation: This does not implement an iteration contract.

choices.text: Pass the order list to an Iterator node and send each item to nodes inside the loop.
choices.explanation: An Iterator can iterate over the items in an array.

choices.text: Poll CloudTrail.
choices.explanation: This does not implement array processing in a Flow.

choices.text: Append each result to the system prompt.
choices.explanation: This does not provide structured aggregation.

choices.text: Use a Collector node to aggregate each Iterator output and pass the results downstream.
choices.explanation: A Collector combines outputs from iterations.

title: Resume the same Flow execution with the additional input requested by an agent
prompt: An Agent node in a Bedrock Flow requests a department code because information is missing from an application. The application receives the user's answer and needs to continue the pending Flow in the same context. How should it make the second InvokeFlow call?

choices.text: Pass the same executionId and send the answer to the Flow Input node used at the start.
choices.explanation: When resuming a multi-turn execution, the destination for the input is the requesting Agent node's agentInputText.

choices.text: Omit executionId and pass only the department code to the Flow Input node.
choices.explanation: The current execution cannot be identified, so the input is not handled as additional information for the original application.

choices.text: Do not specify an Agent node name; set the department code as the alias name for the call.
choices.explanation: The alias specifies which Flow to invoke; it does not provide runtime input to an Agent node.

choices.text: Pass the same executionId, specify the requesting Agent node's nodeName and nodeInputName=agentInputText, and put the answer in content.document.
choices.explanation: This identifies the pending execution and delivers the answer as additional input to the Agent that requested it.

learning.reason: When the department code is provided, specify the same executionId and the input of the Agent node that requested the additional information. This continues the multi-turn execution without restarting the initial Flow input.

choices.explanation: The existing extraction code can be called through the service integration, and its output can be used by a downstream node.

choices.text: Set the extraction function's ARN as the model ID for a Prompt node.

choices.text: Connect the S3 key string from the Flow Input node directly to the body variable.
choices.explanation: An S3 key refers to the extracted text; it is not the text read from the referenced object.

learning.reason: Call the existing extraction function from a Lambda function node in the Flow. Pass the S3 key from the Flow input, and connect the function's output to the Prompt.

choices.explanation: This does not account for variations in execution time.

category: 実装と統合

title: Let a Map Finish Despite Some Record Failures
prompt: You are processing a large number of independent records in a Map state. You want to record a small number of malformed records for later reprocessing and prevent the entire workflow from stopping at the first failure. Which two actions should you take?

choices.text: Set ToleratedFailureCount or Percentage on the Map state
choices.explanation: The Map can continue when failures are within the tolerated limit.

choices.text: Set every Task retry policy to retry indefinitely
choices.explanation: The workflow might never finish if a failure is permanent.

choices.text: Replace the Map state with a Parallel state
choices.explanation: This is not suitable for a large, dynamically sized set of items.

choices.text: Use Catch to route failed records to failure handling
choices.explanation: A Catch in a Task inside the child workflow can record the failed record and transition to `Fail`, so the child failure is counted toward the Map's tolerated-failure threshold. A Catch on the Map itself does not replace per-record isolation.

choices.text: Delete failed records from CloudTrail
choices.explanation: This would lose information needed for reprocessing.

learning.reason: Failure tolerance and Catch can isolate failures for independent items.
learning.concept: Distributed Map failure tolerance

choices.text: Perform Model customization
choices.explanation: Model customization is not a substitute for hosting an agent.

choices.text: Deploy to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime
choices.explanation: AgentCore Runtime runs agents in a managed environment.

choices.explanation: CloudFront is not an agent runtime environment.

title: Apply a retention change to raw events
prompt: An operation currently retains raw conversation events in AgentCore Memory for 60 days. The policy is changing: apply a 30-day retention period to new conversations, while leaving raw events already written with their existing expiration times. Do not change extracted long-term memories. Which option should be chosen?

choices.text: Update recordExpiryDurationDays in the long-term memory strategy to 30 days.
choices.explanation: This setting applies to extracted long-term memories; it does not change the expiration period for raw events when they are collected.

choices.text: Update eventExpiryDuration for short-term memory to 30 days.
choices.explanation: The expiration time for a raw event is determined when it is written, so existing events retain the value set at write time.

choices.text: Delete all existing raw events, then embed the number of days in the short-term memory actor ID.
choices.explanation: This would not retain existing events, and the actor ID does not specify an expiration period.

choices.text: Change the Runtime session idle timeout to 30 days.
choices.explanation: The lifecycle of a runtime session is separate from the expiration time of events already stored in Memory.

learning.reason: Change the short-term memory retention period for new raw events, while relying on existing events to keep the expiration times set when they were written.
learning.concept: In AgentCore Memory, the expiration time for a raw event is determined at write time and is independent of the per-strategy expiration setting for long-term memories.

category: 実装と統合

title: Retrieve semantically similar past cases
prompt: An agent needs to refer to past cases similar to a user's current concern without relying on exact keyword matches. Which Memory Strategy is the best fit?

choices.text: Use only the summary strategy.
choices.explanation: Its main purpose is summarizing conversations, which does not meet the similar-case retrieval requirement.

title: Comparing inference configurations for the same model with load tests
prompt: You are deploying the same model and container to SageMaker AI and have several instance candidates. Before production, you want to compare candidates using representative inputs to find a configuration that meets throughput and latency requirements and offers the best cost efficiency. Which option avoids manually launching a separate load test for each instance?

choices.text: Use Inference Recommender to run load tests for inference configurations automatically, then compare measured latency, throughput, and cost.
choices.explanation: It can evaluate multiple instance configurations for the same model so you can select one that meets your requirements.

choices.text: Change the model's approval status in Model Registry and choose the instance launched with the default settings.
choices.explanation: Approval status does not run load tests or let you compare performance across candidates.

choices.text: Deploy just one type of production endpoint and configure automatic scaling; other instance types will then be compared automatically.
choices.explanation: Scaling changes the amount of active capacity. It is not a load test that compares different deployed instance types.

choices.text: Quantize the model first and treat all unmeasured instance candidates as equivalent.
choices.explanation: This changes the model itself, so it does not compare configuration performance for the original model.

learning.reason: Keep the model and inputs fixed, vary the inference environment by candidate, and compare cost and performance against the requirements.
learning.concept: Inference Recommender automates load testing of SageMaker serving configurations.

choices.text: Run the two independent calls in parallel and pass their results to the model after both complete.

title: Diagnose a 429 as a possible quota limit
prompt: A Bedrock call returns a 429 ThrottlingException. The input format has not changed, and no 503 errors are occurring. What should you check first?

choices.text: Extend the S3 log retention period.
choices.explanation: This does not increase inference quotas.

choices.text: Check the request and token quotas for the model in question, along with actual utilization.
choices.explanation: Correct. ThrottlingException indicates that an account quota or rate limit has been exceeded.

choices.text: Remove the request body as if this were a 400 input-format error.
choices.explanation: This is a different error from an input constraint violation.

choices.text: Start a human evaluation job.
choices.explanation: This does not resolve request throttling.

learning.reason: A 429 indicates a rate or quota limit has been exceeded, so compare usage with the applicable limits.
