title: Capture input and output samples to investigate inference regressions
prompt: In an account that uses SageMaker Model Monitor, you need to investigate a regression in an existing real-time classification endpoint. You want to record future invocations so you can compare inputs with outputs when a prediction is reported as incorrect. However, a data-storage limit means that only 10% may be retained in an approved S3 bucket. Which actions should you take? (Select two.)

choices.text: Set CaptureOptions to Output only and reconstruct the input body from the output.
choices.explanation: In general, the input features or original body cannot be reconstructed from a prediction.

choices.text: Add an alarm for the ModelLatency metric and attach each request and response body to the alarm.
choices.explanation: A metric alarm does not record invocation input and output bodies.

choices.text: Enable DataCaptureConfig on the endpoint and set the sampling percentage to 10% and the destination to the approved S3 bucket.
choices.explanation: This captures a sample of inference requests at the specified destination without retaining every request.

choices.text: Copy 10% of the training data to S3 and treat it as the inference history of the deployed model.
choices.explanation: Training inputs do not show the correspondence between inputs and outputs while the endpoint is running.

choices.text: Set CaptureOptions to both Input and Output.
choices.explanation: This captures the input and output of the selected invocations for analysis.

learning.reason: Store pairs of inputs and outputs from live invocations using endpoint data capture with sampling enabled.
learning.concept: SageMaker DataCaptureConfig specifies the destination, sampling percentage, and whether to capture inputs, outputs, or both.

title: Verify service-role permissions for a human evaluation job
prompt: When you create a human model evaluation job, access to the evaluation S3 bucket is denied. Which check is most appropriate to determine whether the permissions used by the Bedrock service to run the job are missing, rather than a problem with the evaluator portal?

choices.text: Clear only the evaluator's browser history.
choices.explanation: This does not address missing S3 permissions for the Bedrock service role.

choices.text: Disable model invocation logging.
choices.explanation: This is unrelated to the evaluation job's S3 permissions.

choices.text: Move the evaluation data to CloudTrail events.
choices.explanation: CloudTrail events are not suitable for the human evaluation dataset or output destination.

choices.text: Verify that the service role trusting Bedrock can access both the S3 bucket containing the prompt dataset and the S3 bucket for result output.
choices.explanation: Correct. The Bedrock service role for human evaluation needs permission to invoke the selected model and access the input and output S3 buckets.

learning.reason: The Bedrock service role for human evaluation needs access to the selected model and to the S3 locations for prompts and results.
learning.concept: Validating the service role and S3 permissions for human model evaluation

title: Compare evaluation job results programmatically
prompt: You want to compare not only the metrics from two automated model evaluation jobs, but also which prompts produced different results. Which artifact should you examine after evaluation is complete?

choices.text: Read only the CloudTrail management events.
choices.explanation: They do not provide case-level scores for the evaluation results.

choices.text: Rely only on the temporary display in the test UI.
choices.explanation: This does not provide a reproducible comparison.

choices.text: Delete the model to preserve the results.
choices.explanation: This is unrelated to analyzing the results.

choices.text: Analyze the JSONL results by model and dataset saved to the specified S3 output destination.
choices.explanation: Correct. Automated evaluation results are saved as JSONL in S3 and can be used for case-by-case comparisons.

title: Meet the Output Bucket Requirements for Human Evaluation
prompt: You created a human Model Evaluation, but the job fails during preparation because evaluators cannot access the output data from the evaluator interface. Select the two settings required for human evaluation that differ from automated evaluation.

choices.text: Configure CORS so that the model's accuracy improves automatically.
choices.explanation: CORS controls browser access; it does not improve model quality.

choices.text: Configure the required CORS settings on the S3 bucket used for human-evaluation output.
choices.explanation: Correct. Human evaluation requires CORS on the S3 output bucket.

choices.text: Move the input data to CloudTrail.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the data-preparation requirements for human evaluation.

choices.text: Assign human evaluators who meet the evaluation criteria.
choices.explanation: Correct. Human evaluation collects ratings or preferences from evaluators.

choices.text: Disable model invocation logging.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the CORS or human-evaluator requirements.

learning.reason: AWS documentation explains that automated evaluation does not require CORS, whereas human evaluation requires CORS on the output S3 bucket.
learning.concept: Operational prerequisites that differ between human and automated evaluation

title: Resolve a Configuration Conflict When Invoking a Managed Prompt
prompt: You specified the ARN of a prompt created with Prompt management as the Converse modelId, but the application also sent inferenceConfig and failed. When the prompt manages the inference settings, what is the most appropriate fix?

choices.text: Move the same settings to requestMetadata.
choices.explanation: requestMetadata provides invocation tags; it does not specify inference configuration.

choices.text: Put the prompt ARN in the request body as a string and use a different model for modelId.
choices.explanation: This would not invoke the managed prompt.

choices.text: Remove inferenceConfig from the Converse request and use the settings defined in the managed prompt.
choices.explanation: Correct. When using a managed prompt with Converse, certain fields, including inferenceConfig, cannot be included in the request.

choices.text: Increase the retention period for CloudWatch Logs.
choices.explanation: This does not resolve the API request field constraint.

learning.reason: When invoking a Prompt management prompt with Converse, fields such as inferenceConfig cannot be included in the request.
learning.concept: Validating the contract between a managed prompt and Converse request settings

title: Reproduce a Test for a Prompt with Variables
prompt: A prompt template has variables for a customer name and contract type, and only a particular combination produces an unnatural response. What is the best way to investigate this reproducibly with Prompt management?

choices.text: Replace all variables with fixed strings and update production.
choices.explanation: This does not investigate the problematic values and also removes flexibility.

choices.text: Use CloudTrail alone to judge the quality of generated responses.
choices.explanation: Management events do not provide response-quality comparisons.

choices.text: Enter the problematic values as test variables and run the prompt, then compare results across variants as needed.
choices.explanation: Correct. Prompt management lets you run and compare prompts under the same conditions by supplying test values for variables.

choices.text: Maximize the temperature without testing.
choices.explanation: This could make responses less stable.

learning.reason: Prompt management lets you run prompts with test values for variables and compare variants.
learning.concept: Reproducible prompt testing with fixed combinations of variable values

choices.text: Select ProfessionalStyleAndTone (professionalism and style) alone.
choices.explanation: A polite style does not detect omitted requests.

choices.text: Measure only the S3 size of the output file.
choices.explanation: File size does not indicate how completely the response addresses the requests.

choices.text: Measure only CPU utilization in CloudWatch.
choices.explanation: This does not measure the completeness of generated content.

choices.text: Select Completeness.
choices.explanation: Correct. Completeness measures how well a response answers each part of a question.

learning.reason: Completeness evaluates the extent to which a response addresses all parts of a question.

title: Canary deployment with automatic rollback to the previous model
prompt: A generative AI application uses a SageMaker AI real-time endpoint, and you are replacing its current model with a new one. To avoid downtime, you want to route a small portion of production requests to the new model first. If the error rate rises during the observation period, the endpoint should revert to the previous model without waiting for an operator. Which two choices should you make?

choices.text: Specify a canary deployment strategy for a blue/green update, route some traffic to the new environment, and set an observation period.
choices.explanation: You can verify the new environment with a portion of requests before shifting the rest of the traffic.

choices.text: Only change the production variant weights for the old and new models, then email the operations team.
choices.explanation: This adjusts traffic, but it does not manage observation or automatic rollback when an anomaly occurs.

choices.text: Set a CloudWatch alarm on the error rate as an automatic rollback condition for the update.
choices.explanation: If an anomaly in the new environment reaches the threshold, traffic can automatically return to the previous environment.

choices.text: Terminate all instances of the old endpoint before starting the update, then resume requests after the new environment starts.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the availability requirement or preserve the old environment for an immediate rollback.

choices.text: Change only the approval status in Model Registry, without configuring endpoint traffic controls.
choices.explanation: Registry approval does not shift traffic or monitor the endpoint during an update.

learning.reason: Configure the update policy to use a canary shift and a CloudWatch-based rollback.
learning.concept: SageMaker deployment guardrails include observation during a traffic shift and automatic rollback.

title: Rewrite a short prompt for the destination model
prompt: A short English prompt classifies billing inquiries, and you want to use it with another compatible Bedrock model. You want to preserve the prompt currently used by the application, create candidate rewrites suited to the destination model with minimal effort, and compare them with the original. You do not yet have an evaluation dataset. Which option should you choose?

choices.text: Optimize the source model and assume that its model-specific result will maintain the same quality on the destination model.
choices.explanation: The destination model is not the target of the optimization, so this does not meet the goal of generating candidates for it.

choices.text: Fine-tune the new model's weights without generating prompt rewrite candidates.
choices.explanation: Model tuning does not meet the goal of reviewing and comparing rewritten versions of the existing text.

choices.text: Automatically expand the prompt to the destination model's context limit and apply it to production immediately.
choices.explanation: This does not provide candidate wording tailored to the specified model for comparison, and it does not preserve the existing production text.

choices.text: Give the current text to Bedrock's simple prompt optimization, select the destination model as the target, and compare the rewritten candidates it returns.
choices.explanation: It can rewrite a single short prompt for the specified model. You can generate candidates without an evaluation dataset.

learning.reason: Generate rewrite candidates using only the existing prompt text and the destination model, then evaluate them separately before deciding whether to adopt one.
learning.concept: Bedrock simple prompt optimization returns rewrite candidates tailored to the model selected as the target.

title: Update external data items individually while preserving document IDs
prompt: An operations team registers announcements from an internal CMS in a Bedrock Knowledge Bases custom data source. The announcements are revised article by article, and each has a fixed ID in the CMS. How can the team reflect only revised articles in the index without exporting all items to S3 each time, while ensuring that an article's old content is no longer returned as a candidate?

choices.text: Issue a new custom document ID for every revision and leave the old version in place.
choices.explanation: Different IDs are treated as separate documents, so the old content remains a candidate.

choices.text: Specify the document ID in a Retrieve call, then add the changed body to the generation prompt.
choices.explanation: Retrieval and generation alone do not update the documents registered in the knowledge base.

choices.text: Resync the entire S3 data source and do not manage document IDs for the custom data source.
choices.explanation: This does not update the current custom data source item by item and requires exporting all documents.

choices.text: Pass the revised body and the same custom document ID as the existing article to IngestKnowledgeBaseDocuments.
choices.explanation: You can replace the content of a document by supplying its existing ID.

learning.reason: Use the ID managed by the external source during ingestion to update the content of the same article individually.
learning.concept: Direct ingestion into a custom data source replaces the document that has the same ID.

title: Start training without copying all S3 data first
prompt: A company uses existing SageMaker AI training code that reads large training shards in sequence from S3 using file paths. It wants to avoid downloading all the data in advance while keeping the existing code that opens the data as POSIX files. Which change requires the least effort?

choices.text: Set the input channel to File mode.
choices.explanation: Training files are downloaded to storage before the training container starts.

choices.text: Switch to Pipe mode and open the current file names as arbitrary files.
choices.explanation: Pipe streams data through named pipes, which differs from the existing file-reading convention.

choices.text: Add a preprocessing job that syncs the S3 data to local storage each time.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to avoid a full copy in advance and adds another processing step.

choices.text: Switch the S3 input channel to FastFile mode.
choices.explanation: The data remains available as files, and the requested ranges are read from S3, avoiding a full copy in advance.

learning.reason: When you need to preserve existing sequential reads, choose FastFile, which exposes S3 data as files.
learning.concept: FastFile preserves the POSIX read interface and reads S3 data as needed.

title: Using Machine-Checkable Business Rules as Rewards for Additional Training
prompt: The supported Bedrock model can extract fields from purchase orders, but it makes errors when checking whether the total amount agrees with the line items. It is difficult to create many additional reference answers for each response, but the consistency of multiple generated fields can be scored numerically as a unit test. Which approach directly uses this score for additional model training?

choices.text: Record only a numeric reward in the output field for supervised fine-tuning.
choices.explanation: The model would learn the reward as the desired output instead of learning the desired response, so this does not provide the requested scoring method.

choices.text: Use Bedrock reinforcement fine-tuning and specify a Lambda reward function that scores outputs according to the rules.
choices.explanation: This scores generated candidates using deterministic business rules and uses the scores as training rewards.

choices.text: Use Guardrails to block all outputs at runtime and configure the number of blocked outputs as the training job's output file.
choices.explanation: A runtime filter does not provide a way to pass candidate-specific scores into training.

choices.text: Add the consistency rules as documents to a search index and retrieve them without updating the model weights.
choices.explanation: The rules can be added to the prompt, but this does not meet the requirement to use scores for additional model training.

learning.reason: When generated results can be scored automatically, use those scores as rewards for additional training.
learning.concept: Reinforcement fine-tuning assigns rewards to candidate outputs.

title: Separate Reprocessed Data from Existing Valid Output
prompt: A Glue job that creates training data uses bookmarks to track processed input in S3. Some past runs applied incorrect column transformations, so you need to reprocess the data covered by those runs. Preserve valid downstream data and avoid appending the same rows twice to the existing target. Which two actions should you take?

choices.text: Only rewind the bookmark and let Glue delete the reprocessed data from the existing target.
choices.explanation: Bookmarks do not track or delete output.

choices.text: Rewind the job bookmark using a past run corresponding to the target period, then reprocess that data.
choices.explanation: This returns the bookmark tracking state to a past run and limits the scope of reprocessing.

choices.text: Keep the same output location and have the reprocessing job append all source data again.
choices.explanation: The original output remains, and duplicate data is appended.

choices.text: Use the target bucket's lifecycle configuration to delete all current objects before validating the results.
choices.explanation: This would also delete valid data and would not preserve existing downstream use.

choices.text: Write the reprocessed output to a separate location, compare the results, and replace only the affected scope.
choices.explanation: Rewinding does not delete existing output, so separating the output avoids duplicates.

learning.reason: Rewinding affects input tracking; existing output must be handled separately.
learning.concept: Rewinding a Glue bookmark does not delete existing target files.

title: Prevent Stale Ingestion When Notifications Arrive Out of Order
prompt: When a product document in S3 is updated, custom preprocessing updates a search manifest. The same key is rewritten in quick succession, and an older event arrives later and overwrites the newer state. Which approach uses notification data to determine the update order for the same key?

choices.text: Store the last processed sequencer for each object key, and apply an event only when its hexadecimal value is greater.
choices.explanation: For the same key, the relative values of sequencers indicate the event order.

choices.text: Share one sequencer across the entire bucket and accept a notification for any key only if its value exceeds the previous value.
choices.explanation: Sequencers cannot be used to compare event order across different keys.

choices.text: Apply the most recently received notification unconditionally.
choices.explanation: The order of receipt is not guaranteed to match the order in which events occurred.

choices.text: Compare request IDs as strings and treat the larger ID as newer.
choices.explanation: Request IDs are not values for ordering object updates.

learning.reason: Track update revisions per S3 key and use the sequencer for that same key to discard already-processed events.
learning.concept: S3 event notification sequencers can be used to compare the order of events for the same object key.

title: Assign Multiple Classification Labels to One Request Document
prompt: Later summaries must be aggregated by business area, so a customer inquiry can receive multiple custom categories at the same time, such as "billing" and "shipping." You want to use training data that has been manually assigned multiple labels and preserve those labels during preprocessing. Which Amazon Comprehend training mode should you use?

choices.text: Train a custom classifier in multi-class mode, which always assigns one document to exactly one category.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement for multiple categories to apply to the same document.

choices.text: Read errorRecordCount from the output manifest and resubmit that number of records from the beginning of the input JSONL file.

title: Reevaluating a known agent failure from existing traces
prompt: There are three Amazon Bedrock AgentCore trace IDs for an inquiry that received an inaccurate response in production. You want to isolate the cause by applying evaluation criteria only to those traces, without repeating the original tool calls. Which approach is most appropriate?

choices.text: Create an AgentCore online evaluation and sample new traffic unrelated to the target traces.
choices.explanation: This monitors new traffic; it is not a way to select and evaluate the three identified past executions.

choices.text: Specify the relevant trace IDs or span IDs in an AgentCore on-demand evaluation.
choices.explanation: This lets you select and evaluate only the executions under investigation from existing traces or spans.

choices.text: Calculate the average latency for all requests in CloudWatch.
choices.explanation: This may show performance, but it cannot evaluate the accuracy of a specific saved response.

choices.text: Send the same input to a new session in AgentCore Runtime and compare the resulting trace.
choices.explanation: This repeats the original tool behavior in a new execution, so it does not meet the requirement to use only the existing records.

title: Make deployment decisions only after candidate model evaluation succeeds
prompt: A CI pipeline that reruns a Bedrock automatic evaluation reads reports from a shared S3 prefix used by previous jobs, and may deploy a model even when the current evaluation fails. Which change detects failure and bases the deployment decision only on the results of the current rerun?

choices.text: Use the job ARN returned when the current job is created to call GetEvaluationJob, and read the current output only after the status is Completed.
choices.explanation: This identifies the evaluation job and verifies its success, while preventing reports from an older job from affecting the deployment decision.

choices.text: Proceed if there is at least one S3 object whose prefix matches the evaluation job name.
choices.explanation: An object from a previous job could also meet this condition, so it does not prove that the current evaluation succeeded.

choices.text: Treat the evaluation as successful when the creation timestamp of an S3 object for the input evaluation dataset is updated.
choices.explanation: This shows that data was uploaded, but does not show that the candidate model evaluation succeeded.

choices.text: As soon as the job is no longer InProgress, read the latest report from the shared prefix.
choices.explanation: Failed or stopped jobs also have a status other than InProgress, and the latest report could still be from a previous job.

learning.reason: Identify the run using the ARN returned when the evaluation starts, and require Completed as the success condition. Limit the report passed to deployment to output from that same run.

title: Investigating container errors in SageMaker inference
prompt: A valid InvokeEndpoint request to SageMaker AI real-time inference returns ModelError. Without increasing production invocations, you want to narrow down the cause by referring to the status the container actually returned and the corresponding logs. What should you check in the response? Select two.

choices.text: Treat the HTTP status for ModelError as the container's return value and discard the original message.
choices.explanation: The wrapper's 424 alone does not tell you whether the container returned a 4xx or 5xx status.

choices.text: Check OriginalStatusCode and OriginalMessage.
choices.explanation: These distinguish the HTTP status and content returned by the container from the wrapper's HTTP status in SageMaker AI.

choices.text: Handle it like ModelNotReadyException and send the same input until the maximum retry count is reached.
choices.explanation: This does not investigate the details of the current failure and conflicts with the requirement to narrow it down using the existing response and logs.

choices.text: Interpret the response's InvokedProductionVariant as the status returned by the container.
choices.explanation: The variant identifies the inference target; it does not represent the original HTTP status or execution logs.

choices.text: Use LogStreamArn to check the corresponding CloudWatch Logs stream.
choices.explanation: The stream indicated by ModelError can be used to investigate the target inference container's logs.

learning.reason: OriginalStatusCode and OriginalMessage in ModelError provide information from the container, and LogStreamArn can be used to investigate the related logs.
learning.concept: Correlating the original response and logs for InvokeEndpoint ModelError

title: Create point-in-time training data without affecting traffic
prompt: A live support-ticket table in DynamoDB has point-in-time recovery enabled. You want to prepare an S3 dataset for reproducing a generative AI evaluation from all items that existed at an approved baseline time last night. You must not consume production read capacity, and you will select the data after export. Which method is appropriate?

choices.text: Save only a DynamoDB incremental export whose end time is the baseline time.
choices.explanation: An incremental export includes items changed during the specified period, so unchanged items are not included.

choices.text: Run a DynamoDB full export to S3 for the specified baseline time.
choices.explanation: This asynchronously exports the whole table from the specified point in time within the retention period to S3 without consuming the table's read capacity.

choices.text: Read pages with Scan using strong consistency and write each page to S3.
choices.explanation: This uses production table read capacity. The pages do not form a snapshot of the table at one point in time.

choices.text: Read Streams at the baseline time and export the results to S3.
choices.explanation: Streams retain item changes and do not provide a complete point-in-time view that includes unchanged items.

learning.reason: To reproduce the whole table at the same point in time for an evaluation, run a full export at a time within the retention period. An incremental export or change stream alone cannot reproduce the complete table.
learning.concept: Choosing between DynamoDB point-in-time full exports and incremental exports

title: Verify that a new consumer can reprocess all historical events
prompt: Inquiry events are stored for a long period, and the entire retention period is reprocessed whenever preprocessing for the response model is updated. Amazon MSK Avro messages include multiple older versions registered in AWS Glue Schema Registry, and a new consumer must be able to read every older version. Compatibility for older consumers reading new events is not required. Which compatibility mode directly meets this requirement?

choices.text: BACKWARD_ALL
choices.explanation: Checks compatibility so that a new consumer can read every stored older version.

choices.text: BACKWARD
choices.explanation: The direction is correct because a new version can read an older one, but this does not check compatibility with every historical version.

choices.text: FORWARD_ALL
choices.explanation: Checks whether consumers of every older version can read the new version. That is the opposite direction from what is required.

choices.text: NONE
choices.explanation: Allows schemas to be registered but does not check whether a new version can read older events.

learning.reason: Use BACKWARD_ALL when a new consumer must read every historical version. Compatibility with only the immediately preceding version is a different requirement from compatibility with all historical versions.
learning.concept: Schema compatibility for reprocessing stored events

title: Apply a late-arriving feature only to history
prompt: In SageMaker Feature Store used for inference routing, the feature for customer A with event time 12:00 is the current online value. Because ingestion was delayed, the 11:00 value for the same record identifier arrives later. Both the online and offline stores are enabled, and the 11:00 value is needed in the training history as an actual observation. What should you do?

choices.text: Change the 11:00 event time to the current processing time before ingestion.
choices.explanation: The older observation would be treated as a new event and could overwrite the current online value.

choices.text: Delete the online record for the customer, then ingest the 11:00 and 12:00 values in order.
choices.explanation: There is no need to delete the online value currently in use; doing so could create an unnecessary gap and affect history.

choices.text: Ingest the record with 11:00 as its event time.
choices.explanation: The online store retains the 12:00 record, while the late-arriving 11:00 value is also stored in the offline history.

choices.text: Discard the 11:00 value and keep only the already registered 12:00 value.
choices.explanation: The online value remains current, but the historical observation needed for training is lost.

learning.reason: The online store determines which value is newer by event time, not arrival order. Keeping the original time for a delayed event lets you retain history without replacing the latest value.
learning.concept: Late-arriving events and event time in Feature Store

title: Compare every vector key in an index without searching

choices.text: Call QueryVectors for each document and repeatedly search for the top candidates.
choices.explanation: Nearest-neighbor candidates depend on similarity and do not guarantee that every key will be enumerated.

choices.text: Enumerate the index with ListVectors and retrieve pages until there is no continuation token.
choices.explanation: This lists the keys in the specified index sequentially, without relying on similarity ranking.

choices.text: Pass document descriptions to GetVectors to retrieve all keys matching those descriptions.

choices.text: Enable returnMetadata for ListVectors.
choices.explanation: This returns the metadata associated with the vectors stored in the index on each page.

choices.text: Get an index list with ListVectorIndexes and construct document IDs from the index names.
choices.explanation: This returns index information, not the individual keys stored in an index.

learning.reason: To enumerate every vector for an audit, use ListVectors pagination rather than similarity search. Enable the metadata setting to compare the results against the inventory.

choices.text: Lower the page rate limit to prevent the crawler from reaching other hosts.
choices.explanation: The rate limit controls retrieval frequency; it does not specify which URLs or hosts are allowed.

learning.reason: To control the approved scope during collection, configure the crawler's host scope and URL patterns.

title: Compare model and template changes separately
prompt: You are adapting a prompt for summarizing customer inquiries in Bedrock Prompt management for a target model. You want to first see the effect of changing only the model while avoiding any impact on the published version already in production. Which is the best initial comparison?

choices.text: Compare prompt variants in draft that differ only by model, using the same template and test variables and corresponding shared inference settings to review the outputs.
choices.explanation: Keeping the test inputs consistent lets you evaluate output differences as a result of changing the candidate model.

choices.text: Change both the model and template in the application that references the production version, and use future customer inquiries for comparison.

choices.text: Test drafts using real cases for the old model and short synthetic inputs for the new model.

choices.text: Create a new version first, then overwrite the old version in production and measure differences using error logs.
choices.explanation: This is not a draft comparison that preserves the old version in production, and error logs alone cannot assess output quality.

learning.reason: Limit the changed factor to the model and use the same test variables in a draft comparison in Prompt management. Replacing the production version is unnecessary for validation.

title: Combine compressed candidate search with full-precision rescoring
prompt: You operate a vector index for an FAQ in OpenSearch Service, and the cost of keeping full-precision vectors in memory is a concern. Evaluation allows additional reads from storage, and you want to recalculate candidate rankings at the original precision. How should you configure the supported index?

choices.text: Use on_disk mode to select candidates from compressed vectors, then rescore the final candidates using full-precision vectors on disk.
choices.explanation: This reduces memory use for candidate selection while allowing the selected candidates to be reevaluated at full precision.

choices.text: Keep in_memory mode and increase the interval between S3 snapshots.
choices.explanation: Changing backup frequency does not change vector memory usage during search.

choices.text: Use only compressed distances in on_disk mode to determine the final ranking, without rescoring at full precision.
choices.explanation: This may reduce memory use, but it does not meet the requirement to reevaluate rankings at full precision.

choices.text: Scan every candidate with a script and compare every uncompressed vector for each query.
choices.explanation: Unlike a design that reevaluates only candidates narrowed down by approximate search, this increases computation from reading every item.

learning.reason: In the two-stage search of on_disk mode, compressed representations narrow down candidates, and only the selected subset can be rescored at full precision. Evaluate final ranking separately from recall at the candidate-selection stage.
learning.concept: How OpenSearch on_disk search relates memory use to rescoring

title: Restricting an execution role to invoking only the approved agent alias
prompt: The same Bedrock agent has two aliases: one for testing and one for production. choices.text: Allow bedrock:InvokeAgent on all resources and set the production ID in the application configuration.
choices.explanation: The default configuration selects production, but the IAM permission would still allow invocation if the testing alias were specified by mistake.

choices.text: Allow bedrock:UpdateAgentAlias on the production alias.
choices.explanation: This is an alias update operation; it does not allow invocation for inference.

choices.text: Specify only the production agent-alias ARN as the resource for bedrock:InvokeAgent.
choices.explanation: InvokeAgent can specify the resource for the alias being invoked. This limits the permission to the production alias.

choices.text: Allow bedrock:InvokeModel on the production alias ARN.
choices.explanation: Model inference and agent invocation are different actions. The resource type is also incompatible.

learning.reason: Even when the production and testing aliases refer to the same agent, the execution role's permission can be scoped to the production alias.

title: Reusing Cached Responses Only for the Same Published Summary Version and Language
prompt: The content of a summary of a published manual is determined by the document ID, version, and output language. It does not vary by user or permissions, and each version remains unchanged after publication. These three values are sent as parameters to the same API Gateway GET method. choices.text: Use only the document ID as the cache key, and set a short TTL.

choices.text: Use the version and output language as the key, and have Lambda validate the document ID.
choices.explanation: Lambda is not invoked on a cache hit, so it cannot prevent a value for another document from being returned afterward.

choices.text: Enable method response caching and include the document ID, version, and output language in the cache key.

title: Match inference IDs to ground-truth records to measure model quality
prompt: You operate SageMaker Model Monitor model quality monitoring for an existing customer. The caller specifies an inferenceId for each inference, and it is recorded in the capture. choices.text: Record the same value as the corresponding captured inferenceId in eventMetadata.eventId for each label row.
choices.explanation: When the capture includes an inferenceId, that value takes precedence as the join key.

choices.text: Pair labels and predictions saved during the same time window according to the order of their S3 filenames.
choices.explanation: Arrival order or filename order cannot uniquely associate a specific inference with its actual ground truth.

choices.text: Use only the automatically generated eventId on the capture side and ignore the existing inferenceId.
choices.explanation: When an inferenceId exists, that value is used, so the assumption that eventId will be used is incorrect.

choices.text: Write the model's prediction itself to S3 as the label so it can be joined.
choices.explanation: Treating a prediction as ground truth does not let you evaluate the model's actual quality.

learning.reason: When the caller supplies an inference ID, the identifier on the label must match it. Even if a label arrives later, the prediction can then be compared with the ground truth for the same event.

title: Narrowing the evidence passed to generation while retaining a broad candidate set
prompt: In a RAG workflow using Bedrock Knowledge Bases, the relevant evidence can fall below the top four results in the initial search. At the same time, the token budget limits the evidence passed to generation to at most four results. The existing model can score each candidate's relevance to the question independently. Select two configuration choices that allow an initial search of 30 results and a final set of four.

choices.text: Set numberOfResults for the initial vector search to 30.
choices.explanation: This allows evidence lower in the initial ranking to be considered as a candidate before relevance is reassessed.

choices.text: Leave the initial numberOfResults at 4 and set the number of reranking results to 30.
choices.explanation: Documents not retrieved by the initial search are not included as candidates. Increasing only the result count does not improve the initial search's recall.

choices.text: Retrieve 30 results and pass them all to generation, then set the model's maxTokens to 4.
choices.explanation: This limits the maximum output tokens; it does not limit the input evidence to four results.

choices.text: Specify a supported model in the vector search reranking configuration and set numberOfRerankedResults to 4.
choices.explanation: After the broad candidate set is rescored for relevance to the question, it can be narrowed to the top four.

choices.text: Retrieve 30 results, then select the first four in the initial ranking without rescoring them.
choices.explanation: This provides no opportunity for evidence ranked fifth or lower initially to move up after reassessment.

learning.reason: The initial retrieval count and the number of results returned after rescoring can be configured separately. This lets you keep a broad candidate set while using only a small number of question-relevant evidence items.

prompt: Batch-transcribe a meeting recording with Amazon Transcribe and prepare the utterances for RAG. Have a person review only the audio segments corresponding to low-confidence words, while retaining punctuation items and the rest of the transcript. Which processing step is appropriate?

choices.text: For pronunciation items in the output's items, compare candidate confidence values numerically and send words below the threshold for review using their start_time and end_time.
choices.explanation: The confidence of each pronunciation candidate can be mapped to its time segment in the recording.

choices.text: Use speaker labels to identify meeting participants and assign the same confidence level to every word spoken by a given participant.
choices.explanation: Speaker labels do not indicate the recognition confidence of each word or narrow down which words need correction.

choices.text: Count punctuation marks in the full transcript string and treat every sentence containing punctuation as low confidence.
choices.explanation: Punctuation does not correspond to word recognition confidence and cannot identify an audio segment.

choices.text: Ignore recording timestamps and send the entire meeting for reprocessing if even one low-confidence value appears.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to check timestamps for low-confidence words and review only part of the recording.

learning.reason: Pronunciation items have start and end times and candidate confidence values. Treat punctuation separately to narrow down which segments need audio review while keeping the rest usable.

choices.text: Simply raise the minimum relevance score for the same user.

choices.text: Give the search application's execution role read access to all documents and omit each user's conditions.
choices.explanation: Permission for a service to search the index differs from an individual user's permission to view a document.

title: Focus the budget on promising hyperparameter candidates
prompt: During training of a generative AI evaluation model, an objective metric is reported at the end of each epoch, and poor-performing configurations can be identified from their early progress. There is not enough budget to run every configuration up to the maximum number of epochs. Which method compares short training runs and continues only promising configurations for longer?

choices.explanation: This systematically enumerates candidates, but it does not reallocate training resources among them based on intermediate results.

choices.text: Use Hyperband with SageMaker automatic model tuning, specifying the objective metric and the range of training resources for each rung.
choices.explanation: It stops poorly performing candidates based on intermediate results and assigns more training resources to promising candidates.

choices.text: Choose Random and set the maximum number of epochs for every trial so that all trials run to completion.
choices.explanation: This samples candidates, but it is designed to run even poorly performing candidates to the end.

choices.text: Use only one previously tested configuration and collect no objective metrics during training.
choices.explanation: This reduces compute, but it does not compare multiple candidates or reallocate resources to promising ones.

learning.reason: When intermediate training metrics are available and the tuning budget is limited, Hyperband uses results from shorter runs to determine subsequent resource allocation.

choices.explanation: This distributes input by S3 object and reduces the input storage required on each instance.

title: Exclude features learned after prediction time from the training set
prompt: You are training a classifier to predict AI routing from information available when a past inquiry occurred. The ground-truth labels have event timestamps, and the feature group also retains customer aggregates updated at a later date as historical records. Which join method should you use to prevent future information from leaking into the inputs?

choices.text: Join the latest online features to every historical label in the same way.
choices.explanation: This can bring values from future updates into the past.

choices.text: Match labels and features by customer ID, and perform a point-in-time join that uses the latest feature record available no later than each label's event time.
choices.explanation: This reproduces only the features available at the time of each label and excludes later updates from the training input.

choices.text: Keep only the most recent row for each customer from the offline features and join without a time condition.
choices.explanation: Moving the data to offline storage does not add a condition that excludes records created after the training point in time.

choices.text: Join the feature values first, then sort the labels and features separately by time.
choices.explanation: Sorting does not align the timestamps row by row and cannot undo a join that used future features.

learning.reason: For training data, join on the same identifier and include only features available before the label's reference time. This differs from joining the latest values.

title: Prepare distillation data using only reviewed teacher responses
prompt: You are distilling a smaller model in Bedrock. You have reviewed responses already generated using the same model version as the teacher model, and the selected invocations are tagged with a purpose in request metadata. You want to use only approved responses for training without having the teacher generate new responses. Choose two components of the configuration.

choices.text: Use prompt-and-response pairs from invocation logs as the training source, and use logs that match the selected teacher model.
choices.explanation: This uses existing responses directly for training and avoids mixing in responses generated by a different teacher model.

choices.text: Use only the prompts from the logs as input and have the teacher model generate responses again.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to use the existing approved responses as is.

choices.text: Filter invocation logs by the purpose in the request metadata.

title: Verify the full-object checksum of a large training archive
prompt: You are uploading a training archive using multipart upload. You received the source file's full-object checksum through a separate channel, and you want S3 to validate the entire object when it is stored. The checksum you received uses CRC64NVME, and the part layout varies from one upload to another. Which option is correct?

choices.text: Directly compare the ETag returned when the multipart upload is completed with the source file's CRC64NVME checksum.
choices.explanation: A multipart ETag is not a full-file checksum computed with the specified algorithm.

choices.text: Validate only the last part and compare that part's value with the full-object value for the source file.
choices.explanation: A value for only part of the file cannot confirm whether the entire file matches.

choices.text: Select CRC64NVME as the full-object checksum for the upload, and provide the source file's checksum value when completing the upload.
choices.explanation: S3 can compare its computed value with the source full-object checksum and fail the upload if they do not match.

choices.text: Store the source value as a string in user-defined S3 metadata only.
choices.explanation: Storing a metadata value alone does not make S3 calculate and validate the received object's full value.

learning.reason: For multipart uploads, distinguish per-part checksums from the full-object checksum. Providing the CRC64NVME full-object checksum lets S3 compare it with the received value regardless of the number of parts or their boundaries.

choices.text: Have the external endpoint return a successful response within 5 seconds after placing the request in a durable queue, and receive completion through a separate notification.

choices.text: Record the request as complete as soon as the event arrives and do not report the external service's result.
choices.explanation: This does not distinguish acceptance from completion or meet the requirement to ingest the final result.

prompt: An EventBridge rule delivers document update events to an SQS FIFO queue. The queue must treat messages for the same document as one group and avoid duplicate registration if the same business update ID is sent again within 5 minutes. Content-based deduplication is disabled, and the target must allow the group and deduplication IDs to be specified when invoked. Select two.

choices.text: Generate and specify a new random ID in MessageGroupId for each delivery attempt.
choices.explanation: Updates to the same document would be split across different groups, preventing the use of ordering within a group.

choices.text: Set the document ID as MessageGroupId.
choices.explanation: This places messages for the same document in the same FIFO message group.

choices.text: Set only the document ID as MessageDeduplicationId.
choices.explanation: This could cause different business updates to the same document to be treated as duplicates.

choices.text: Switch to a standard SQS queue and output only MessageGroupId when receiving messages.
choices.explanation: A standard queue does not provide the FIFO ordering and deduplication required.

choices.text: Set a stable business update ID as MessageDeduplicationId and pass the same value when retrying the delivery.
choices.explanation: For the same business update within the deduplication interval, the FIFO queue can receive the same identifier.

learning.reason: SQS FIFO ordering is managed within each message group. Preserve the deduplication ID when retrying the same business update, and do not reuse it for different updates.
learning.concept: EventBridge FIFO SQS target

choices.text: Increase the index-update Lambda's timeout while keeping the original SQS queue and filter.

choices.text: Have the worker call PostToConnection on the target API Gateway Management API to send the result to the retained connectionId.
choices.explanation: This lets a backend other than the initial route handler send data to a connected client.

learning.concept: API Gateway WebSocket connection identifiers and asynchronous PostToConnection

choices.text: Set a redrive policy on the source SQS queue and specify the maximum receive count and a dead-letter queue.
choices.explanation: Pipes inherits the source queue's DLQ behavior, allowing repeatedly failing messages to be isolated from the original queue.

learning.reason: For a Pipe with an SQS source, specify where messages that could not be retried should go in the SQS source queue's redrive policy.
learning.concept: The DLQ redrive settings inherited by an SQS source for Pipes

title: Prevent External Sharing of AI Data Buckets Across an Organization

choices.explanation: ACLs remain enabled, and this setting does not unconditionally standardize ownership of all objects in the central account.

title: Distribute a model artifact backup standard across an organization

choices.text: Manually create the same policy in each member account.
choices.explanation: This does not use a centrally attached policy that member accounts inherit, so it does not provide ongoing centralized governance.

choices.text: Enable the backup policy type in the organization.

choices.text: Delete CloudTrail to speed up backup processing.

choices.text: Standardize model names to copy them automatically to every account.

choices.text: Create a backup policy in the management account and attach it to the target OU or accounts.

learning.reason: Distribute plans by enabling and attaching backup policies. Keep this separate from trusted access, which is required for organization-wide job monitoring.

choices.text: Use DataZone subscription requests and approval workflows, granting access only to consumers approved by the owner

title: Preserve evidence of an inference under investigation with no set end date

choices.text: Retain the object for one day in Object Lock governance mode
choices.explanation: Protection ends when the configured period expires, so this does not suit an open-ended requirement.

choices.text: Enable S3 Versioning only
choices.explanation: Keeping previous versions does not indefinitely prevent deletion by a principal with the necessary permissions.

choices.text: Set an S3 Object Lock legal hold on the object
choices.explanation: A legal hold has no expiration and prevents deletion or overwriting of the object until it is explicitly removed.

title: Inherit preventive controls in new AI accounts
prompt: You will continue adding accounts for AI workloads to a dedicated OU. You want all current and new accounts to prevent settings that violate organizational policies from being created. Which AWS Control Tower operating model is most appropriate?

choices.text: Manually distribute the same IAM policy to each new account after it is created
choices.explanation: This cannot ensure inheritance or consistent application and does not prevent violations at creation time.

choices.text: Enable detective controls only and remediate after receiving notifications
choices.explanation: Detection evaluates noncompliant resources after they are created, so this does not meet the preventive requirement.

choices.text: Enable preventive controls on the target OU so that accounts under the OU inherit them
choices.explanation: AWS Control Tower preventive controls apply to an OU and prevent noncompliant actions in its member accounts.

choices.text: Only extend the CloudTrail retention period
choices.explanation: This preserves evidence but does not prevent noncompliant settings from being created.

title: Verify the Integrity of AI Configuration Audit Logs

choices.text: Enable only CloudTrail Insights
choices.explanation: Insights detects unusual management event activity; it does not validate log file integrity.

choices.text: Only copy CloudTrail logs to CloudWatch Logs
choices.explanation: Adding a destination does not configure cryptographic integrity validation for the log files.

choices.text: Enable CloudTrail log file integrity validation and verify the files using digest files
choices.explanation: When log file integrity validation is enabled, CloudTrail provides digest files that can be used to verify whether log files have been modified or deleted.

choices.text: Shorten the trail's retention period

choices.explanation: Obscuring a name does not prevent or detect access allowed by a resource policy.

choices.text: Use IAM Access Analyzer external access analysis
choices.explanation: IAM Access Analyzer analyzes resource-based policies and can detect resources that allow access from outside the organization or public access.

title: Reassess Newly Discovered Vulnerabilities in AI Inference Containers
prompt: AI inference container images remain unchanged while stored in ECR for long periods. You want to evaluate the images continuously so that you can also identify vulnerabilities disclosed later. Which Amazon Inspector configuration is most appropriate?

choices.explanation: Amazon Inspector enhanced scanning continuously rescans ECR images and evaluates vulnerabilities that become detectable later.

choices.explanation: Detecting unusual API activity is not an assessment of vulnerabilities in container packages.

title: Automatically Remediate Missing Required Classification Tags on AI Data Buckets
prompt: S3 buckets that store AI data must have the DataClassification tag. If the tag is missing after a bucket is created, you want AWS Config to detect it first and then automatically set an approved default value. Choose two required actions.

choices.explanation: This retains records, but does not evaluate or remediate missing tags.

choices.explanation: Versioning protects object versions; it is separate from evaluating and remediating bucket tag compliance.

title: Identify workloads driving the total input token count
prompt: A generative AI platform records an anonymized workloadId and a numeric inputTokens value in CloudWatch Logs for each invocation. You want to continuously review the top workloads by total input tokens over a given period, rather than by invocation count. How should you configure a Contributor Insights rule?

choices.text: Set workloadId as the Contributor key, inputTokens as the value to sum, and AggregateOn to Sum.
choices.explanation: This groups log events by workload and shows the highest totals independently of invocation count.

choices.text: Use workloadId as the key and set AggregateOn to Count.
choices.explanation: This counts log rows. It does not distinguish the total token volume of workloads with long inputs from those with short inputs.

choices.text: Use inputTokens as the Contributor key and set AggregateOn to Count.
choices.explanation: This counts occurrences for each token-count value, so it does not identify which workloads have the highest usage.

choices.text: Set workloadId as the value to sum and ingest inputTokens only as a string label.
choices.explanation: The workload identifier is not a numeric aggregation target, and the token count would not contribute to the sum.

choices.text: Set the API Gateway usage plan's monthly quota to the contracted amount and treat that value alone as a hard limit.

choices.explanation: New paid inference could begin while the post-call aggregation is delayed.

choices.text: Use the usage plan for ordinary traffic control, and atomically check and reserve the remaining quota in a shared application-side counter before starting inference.
choices.explanation: Because usage plan quotas are best effort, enforce the hard limit separately with concurrency in mind.

choices.text: Rotate the API key to reset the quota for customers using the old key.
choices.explanation: Key rotation does not strictly enforce the quota, and actual inference usage does not necessarily match the remaining contractual quota.

learning.reason: Use a usage plan to guide and control request usage. Enforce a contractual limit that must not be exceeded before inference, with admission logic that prevents concurrent requests from both being accepted against the same remaining quota.

title: Retain execution details for failed asynchronous preprocessing events
prompt: A document-processing Lambda function is invoked directly and asynchronously. To investigate failures after retries, you want a queue to receive the original input along with Lambda execution information and the error returned by the function. Which option meets this requirement?

choices.text: Configure only a function dead-letter queue to obtain the full invocation record.
choices.explanation: A dead-letter queue and an on-failure destination retain different content. The dead-letter queue does not receive the destination record containing the full response.

choices.text: Configure a queue as the asynchronous invocation's OnSuccess destination.
choices.explanation: This destination is for successful invocations; it does not handle processing that fails after retries.

choices.text: Specify a standard SQS queue as the OnFailure destination for Lambda asynchronous invocations.
choices.explanation: The destination receives an invocation record containing the original input and context such as request and response details.

choices.text: Add a setting to return errors in the response to a synchronous invocation while keeping the invocation asynchronous.
choices.explanation: An asynchronous invocation does not return the function's final processing result directly to the caller.

learning.reason: The invocation record sent to a Lambda asynchronous destination includes input and response details. This differs from a dead-letter queue, which primarily retains the input event.
learning.concept: Lambda asynchronous invocation OnFailure destinations and invocation records

choices.text: Reserve On-Demand EC2 instances for dedicated workers and keep them running continuously.

choices.text: Delete the queue and discard incomplete documents when capacity is insufficient.

choices.text: Use the FARGATE_SPOT capacity provider for the ECS service running the workers.
choices.explanation: This uses interruptible spare Fargate capacity to reduce costs without managing instances.

learning.reason: Fargate Spot can be used for retryable background processing. Its key difference from regular Fargate is that interruptions are acceptable.

title: Preserving events that Lambda could not accept on the delivery side
prompt: An EventBridge rule invokes Lambda asynchronously using the EVENT invocation type. The function's invoke permission has been removed, so EventBridge cannot get the function to accept the invocation. Which option preserves events that were not accepted so they can be used to investigate similar delivery failures in the future?

choices.text: Configure only an OnFailure destination for Lambda asynchronous invocations.
choices.explanation: This applies when processing fails after Lambda has accepted the invocation; Lambda cannot retain an event it never accepted.

choices.text: Only increase the Lambda timeout.
choices.explanation: This has no effect on a permission error during delivery, before Lambda processing has started.

choices.text: Configure a standard SQS dead-letter queue for the target on the rule, and grant EventBridge permission to write to it.
choices.explanation: EventBridge isolates events that the function did not accept. When the target lacks permission, the event may be sent directly to the DLQ without retries.

choices.text: Only extend the event's maximum age for the rule, without configuring a queue to store delivery failures.
choices.explanation: Changing the delivery deadline does not provide an isolation destination. When the target lacks permission, retries may not occur.

learning.reason: Failures before an invocation is accepted are isolated on the EventBridge delivery side. Use Lambda-side settings for processing failures after Lambda accepts the invocation asynchronously.

title: Investigate why a vector index has not rolled over
prompt: In OpenSearch Service, a document index has reached its size limit, but it has not rolled over to a new index. The ISM policy and write alias are configured. Which option lets you inspect the state of the policy applied to the index before making changes?

choices.text: Run ISM Explain for the index and check the current policy and state.
choices.explanation: This provides information about the policy applied to the individual index and its progress.

choices.text: Remove the policy from the existing index without waiting for rollover to complete.
choices.explanation: This changes the operational configuration before observing its current state.

choices.text: Stop search writes and infer the policy state from the alias list alone.
choices.explanation: The alias is useful evidence, but it does not show the current ISM state or the operation being performed.

choices.text: Send all searches to another Region and monitor how much is added to the index.
choices.explanation: Observing traffic alone cannot reveal the policy state for the index in question.

learning.reason: Configuring an ISM policy and applying it are different things. Use Explain on the index to inspect its applied state and operation information.
learning.concept: Inspect per-index policy status with OpenSearch Service ISM Explain

examDomain: テスト・検証・トラブルシューティング
title: Tracing Representative Inference Paths Under High Load
prompt: You are using X-Ray to investigate latency from a generative AI application's API through its downstream processing, but recording every request would produce too much trace data. Which setting should you use to retain representative paths needed for root-cause analysis?

choices.text: Disable X-Ray.
choices.explanation: You would not be able to analyze the paths.

choices.text: Use an X-Ray sampling rule to sample a portion of requests.
choices.explanation: Correct. Sampling rules let you control the amount of data recorded while analyzing distributed traces.

choices.text: Delete the logs.
choices.explanation: This reduces the evidence available for investigation.

choices.text: Retrain the model.
choices.explanation: This is unrelated to controlling trace volume.

learning.reason: X-Ray sampling rules control the volume of requests that are recorded.
learning.concept: Optimizing observability through distributed trace sampling.
